articles.summary: Betfair te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Celta y Osasuna en el Estadio de Balaídos correspondiente a la primera jornada de LaLiga
articles.body: El Celta se enfrenta a Osasuna en el Estadio de Balaídos este jueves en el partido correspondiente a la primera jornada de LaLiga 26/27, aunque, igual que ha ocurrido con otros encuentros de este arranque de curso marcado por el calendario del Mundial, no será el estreno liguero de ninguno de los dos. Ambos ya han disputado su primer partido oficial de la temporada. El conjunto gallego no pasó del empate sin goles en su visita a Mestalla ante el Valencia, un duelo muy igualado en el que ninguno de los dos equipos logró imponer su ley pese a las ocasiones de ambos conjuntos de adelantarse en el marcador. Osasuna, por su parte, tampoco pudo estrenar su casillero de victorias. Empató igualmente a cero en El Sadar frente a un Levante que se llevó un punto meritorio a domicilio. Con ambos conjuntos llegando sin goles a favor en su casillero, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Celta por jugar en casa. Betfair paga su triunfo a cuota 1.95, por 3.40 del empate y 4.1 de la victoria de Osasuna. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan invita a la cautela después de lo visto en la primera jornada de los dos conjuntos. Ni el Celta ni Osasuna encontraron el gol en sus respectivos estrenos, y en ambos casos las sensaciones apuntaron más a un problema de definición que a una falta de generación de ocasiones. Esa sequía compartida hace que las apuestas deportivas estén muy igualadas. Betfair paga a 1.88 ambas opciones. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta también hacia un partido de perfil bajo en cuanto a tantos. Ninguno de los dos equipos pasó del empate a cero en su primera jornada, y ambos mostraron una defensa notablemente ordenada frente a rivales con argumentos ofensivos. Esa tendencia hacia lo contenido invita a pensar en un duelo más cerrado que abierto en Balaídos. Betfair sitúa la cuota del -2.5 goles totales a 1.66, por 2.15del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under El mercado de córners también se apoya en lo sucedido en el partido de Liga anterior de cada equipo. Osasuna fue un conjunto muy activo por las bandas en El Sadar, generando hasta 9 saques de esquina frente a los 4 que concedió ante el Levante, una diferencia notable que muestra su vocación de llegar con insistencia por los costados aun sin premio en el marcador. El Celta, por su parte, protagonizó en Mestalla un partido mucho más gris en ese apartado, con pocas llegadas claras por banda y un juego que se resolvió más por dentro que por fuera ante el Valencia.

articles.title: Fuerte temblor de magnitud 5.4 sacude a Colombia este 26 de agosto: sintió en Bogotá y otras ciudades
articles.standfirst: Un fuerte sismo de magnitud 5.4 sacude varias ciudades de Colombia este 26 de agosto
articles.summary: Un fuerte sismo de magnitud 5.4 sacude varias ciudades de Colombia este 26 de agosto
articles.body: Un fuerte sismo de magnitud 5.4 en la escala de Richter se sintió con notable intensidad en gran parte del territorio nacional sobre las 11:45 a. m. de este miércoles 26 de agosto. El evento sísmico, que tuvo una profundidad clasificada como superficial (menor a 30 kilómetros), generó momentos de zozobra en las principales ciudades del país, entre ellas Bogotá, Bucaramanga, Tunja, Medellín y Manizales. Debido a su escasa profundidad, las ondas sísmicas se propagaron con gran fuerza por la superficie, lo que incrementó significativamente la aceleración del terreno y la sacudida en edificaciones de zonas urbanas densamente pobladas. De acuerdo con el boletín oficial emitido por la red de estaciones del Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC), los parámetros técnicos preliminares registran lo siguiente: Aunque el departamento de Santander alberga el conocido "Nido Sísmico de Los Santos" (uno de los puntos con mayor actividad telúrica del planeta), la mayoría de sus eventos ocurren a más de 140 kilómetros de profundidad. En esta oportunidad, al tratarse de un temblor de origen superficial, la energía liberada provocó sacudidas de mayor impacto térmico y sísmico en la corteza. Inmediatamente registrado el temblor, se activaron las alargas en cientos de edificaciónes. En Bogotá, miles de trabajadores, estudiantes y habitantes evacuaron preventivamente edificios corporativos, entidades de gobierno y centros educativos en sectores emblemáticos como el Centro Internacional, la Calle 26, el corredor financiero de la Calle 72 y la Ciudad Universitaria. El cuerpo de Bomberos Oficiales de Bogotá y el IDIGER (Instituto Distrital de Gestión de Riesgos y Cambio Climático) desplegaron rápidamente un barrido de inspección en las 20 localidades de la capital. Según el reporte preliminar de emergencias: En Bucaramanga y municipios aledaños a la zona epicentral (Floridablanca, Girón y Piedecuesta), el temblor se sintió con especial estruendo, provocando la salida inmediata de la ciudadanía a parques y zonas despejadas. La Unidad Nacional para la Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres (UNGRD) activó la Sala de Crisis Nacional para consolidar el reporte de los Consejos Departamentales de Gestión del Riesgo de Santander, Boyacá, Cundinamarca y Antioquia. articles.title: Ramón Jesurún continuará en la presidencia de la FCF hasta 2030 tras ser reelegido
articles.standfirst: Ramón Jesurún es reelegido como presidente de la FCF: estará al mando del fútbol colombiano hasta 2030
articles.summary: Ramón Jesurún es reelegido como presidente de la FCF: estará al mando del fútbol colombiano hasta 2030
articles.body: En una jornada clave para la dirigencia del balompié nacional, la Asamblea de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol oficializó la reelección de Ramón Jesurún como presidente del organismo directivo para el periodo de 2026 a 2030. Con este nuevo mandato, que comenzará de manera oficial el próximo 28 de agosto, Jesurún completará su segundo periodo consecutivo al frente de la institución, consolidando su liderazgo en la administración del fútbol colombiano por cuatro años más. La ratificación de Jesurún estuvo acompañada de la confirmación de la cúpula que lo acompañará en la toma de decisiones. El Comité Ejecutivo para el nuevo ciclo quedó integrado por: Adicionalmente, se conformaron las siete Comisiones Asesoras de la FCF, cuyos miembros desempeñarán sus cargos durante el mismo periodo de cuatro años con el objetivo de brindar respaldo técnico, legal y administrativo a la gestión del nuevo directivo. El nuevo periodo de Ramón Jesurún al frente de la FCF no estará exento de desafíos de alto calibre. Durante los próximos cuatro años, la directiva deberá gestionar eventos estratégicos para el balompié nacional, entre los que destacan la planificación de la Copa América 2028 y el proceso clasificatorio para el Mundial de 2030. Asimismo, la gestión estará bajo la lupa en cuanto al desarrollo del fútbol profesional femenino, el fortalecimiento de las selecciones juveniles y las decisiones administrativas del torneo local.

articles.title: Magnus Carlsen has a lot to teach, he’s one of the best, says Divya Deshmukh
articles.summary: Chess News: Women’s World Cup winner Divya Deshmukh to debut in Global Chess League with Alpine APL Pipers led by Magnus Carlsen; hopes India’s 100th GM is a woman.
articles.body: Nagpur: Women’s World Cup winner Divya Deshmukh will make her Global Chess League (GCL) debut with defending champions Alpine APL Pipers, led by world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen. With a lineup featuring the positional precision of Anish Giri and Vidit Gujrathi, the experience of Koneru Humpy and reigning world rapid champion Volodar Murzin, the addition of 20-year-old Divya makes Pipers one of the strongest contenders in the fourth season of the GCL.Divya is excited to make her debut alongside a well-balanced team. Speaking with TOI, Divya said, “I am very excited that Alpine Pipers chose me and it was the team that I was secretly hoping I would get selected in. So it was a very happy moment for me when I found out that they took me. And I am looking forward to it. I am especially happy about Murzin because we also share a team in World Rapid, Blitz and of course he’s very good.”Divya is also looking forward to learning some tricks from World No. 1 Carlsen, the team leader. “It’s my first time being a teammate with Carlsen. We’ve met before but haven’t interacted much. Now that I’m a teammate, it’s a nice opportunity to learn some things from him. He has a lot to teach and he’s one of the best,” she said.With India on the verge of getting its 100th Grandmaster, Divya is excited. “I don’t know who’s in the running. I’m hoping that there will be more female GMs from India. Right now, I’m hoping that a woman becomes India’s 100th GM.”On adapting with teammates who are also her opponents, Divya said, “It’s not difficult to adapt because I’ve played against them. It feels nice that we will be playing on the same team. And also in the Olympiad, we’ll be playing on the same team. So we’ll be teammates for a month.”On being the youngest Arjuna Awardee, Divya said, “After a shaky year, it was nice to win the Arjuna Award. I just hope to attend the ceremony. I’m hoping it’ll be held in Dec, because in Oct I’ll be representing India and playing GCL in Sept.”Asked about the flexibility of pairings in GCL where a team comprises mixed genders, Divya said, “It’s fun to mix things around. So maybe something like we can have a board order on. Let’s say something like we play on any board and opposite team can do the same. So we can never know the pairing. It would be quite chaotic, but it would be fun.”At her debut appearance in the 2026 Cairns Cup in St Louis, USA, recently, Divya had a strong start but finished tied fifth to seventh. On her overall performance, she said, “It was very average, I would say. I had a good tournament till I lost to Tan (Zhongyi), which was an unfortunate game because I was pressing the whole time and then did not manage my time well and went down on time and ended up making a mistake. Overall the games that I played were actually very good. Since I didn’t feel any pressure I played very good chess.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kameron Johnson shows flashes of something special at kick returner
articles.summary: Breaking down Kameron Johnson Shows Flashes of Something Special at Kick Returner
articles.body:
Kameron Johnson gave the Tampa Bay Buccaneers another encouraging look at what he can bring to the return game Saturday night, showing the type of burst and explosiveness that can make him a difference-maker throughout the 2026 season. Johnson had one kickoff return against the Kansas City Chiefs , taking it 20 yards to the Kansas City 31-yard line and giving Tampa Bay solid starting field position. He also added two punt returns for 24 yards.

The numbers weren't overwhelming, but the flashes were there. Johnson looked decisive with the football in his hands and showed the ability to get north quickly rather than spending too much time searching for an opening. In 2025, he averaged 25.4 yards on 27 kickoff returns and 11.2 yards on 26 punt returns. He also produced Tampa Bay's two longest kick returns of the season, going for 37 and 44 yards, while earning NFC Special Teams Player of the Week honors.

His work against Kansas City was also encouraging because of his offensive contributions. Johnson caught four passes for 56 yards, including a 22-yard reception, while showing that his ability with the ball isn't limited to special teams. He was involved early, catching an 11-yard pass from Jake Browning before later hauling in a 22-yard completion in the third quarter. That combination could make Johnson particularly useful for Tampa Bay. His primary job is returning kicks and punts, but if he continues showing that kind of ability as a receiver, the Buccaneers have another way to get him involved without asking him to become a major part of the offense. If Johnson can consistently turn returns into positive field position while making occasional plays on offense, his value to the Buccaneers could extend well beyond what the traditional returner role offers.

articles.title: Central Texas high school football coaches answer who are the area's best teams and players
articles.summary: Central Texas high school football coaches gave their answers as to who the best teams and players are around the Austin area.
articles.body:
What do Central Texas high school football coaches think of other Austin-area teams and players?

The American-Statesman sent out a questionnaire earlier this month with eight topics to two dozen local coaches. Fifteen responded on the condition their answers would be anonymous. Here are the six questions related to area teams and players with a summary of their answers.

Note: Coaches could not vote for their own players or team. Some coaches didn't answer every question.

What Central Texas team is most likely to win state?

Only four teams received votes, with Lake Travis leading the way with five.

Weiss and Vandegrift both garnered four votes, while Westlake received one vote.

Weiss' Jaxon Schad had the most votes with six, edging Bastrop's Weston Nielsen, who received four. Chase Ames of Dripping Springs garnered two and Cedar Park's David Cooper received one.

Best local player (non-QB) you'll see on your schedule?

Weiss wideout Tre Moore tallied the most votes with four. Hutto wide receiver/defensive back Jaiden Fields was the only other player to receive more than one vote, finishing with two. Lake Travis defensive back Luca Antoun, LBJ running back Marquis Murry II, Manor running back Andre Terry, Legacy Ranch quarterback Drew Langford, Taylor running back Eric Walker, Manor edge Princeton Umanmielen and Round Rock wideout Dylan Jaeger also received votes.

Best local player (non-QB) who isn't on your schedule?

Moore, a Washington commit, and Fields, an Oklahoma pledge, led the way again here with three votes each. Liberty Hill running back Dylan Belinga, Westlake running back CJ Jones, Westlake defensive back Wylie Nichols, Bastrop wideout Dallas Crescenzo and LBJ's Murry all received one vote.

What Austin-area team will surprise this year?

There was no consensus here, with Cedar Ridge, East View and Cedar Park being the only teams to receive more than one vote, with all three getting two. Others cast ballots for Manor, Hedrickson, Dripping Springs, Del Valle, Jarrell, Austin High, Vista Ridge and Bowie.

DeSoto led the way with five votes. Galena Park North Shore garnered three votes, Waxahachie had two votes, and Allen, Smithson Valley and Lake Travis each received one vote.

articles.summary: Tiger Woods made a rare public appearance on Tuesday to celebrate his friend, former pro golfer Notah Begay III, five months after his rollover crash in Flor...
articles.body:
Tiger Woods made a rare public appearance on Tuesday to celebrate his friend, former pro golfer Notah Begay III, five months after his rollover crash in Florida made headlines.

The 50-year-old appeared in a pre-recorded clip sent to his longtime friend to congratulate him on winning the 2026 Payne Stewart Award, and the golfing legend looked almost unrecognizable with gray streaks in his beard and a drawn countenance. He wore a purple polo shirt as he sang Notah's praises and reflected on their decades-long friendship.

"It's been an unbelievable ride with you," he began. "You first came into my life when I was 11 years old, playing in the junior world, and you came to watch me play. Our friendship started there and never ended."

"To see what you've done off the golf course – I know you've won four times on the tour, playing in the Presidents Cup…but to see what you've done off the course and for your local Native American communities, you've helped over 80,000 youths and their families, which is absolutely incredible," he continued.

"There are so many people out there who are struggling in those communities, and you're trying to raise the bar to allow them to go on and achieve a lot more in life and have the successes that I think they deserve and you feel they deserve…Thank you for getting our friendship started, and I love you, dude."

After the clip was posted on social media, fans took to the comment section to exclaim over his unrecognizable look, while others came to his defence. "Man, that's sad," wrote one, while another added: "That is not Tiger Woods."

Learn more about Tiger's arrest below...

Another chimed in: "Love you, Tiger!" and a fourth said: "How about everyone just understanding what we're all wrestling/dealing with and that Tiger is like all of us. Remember what we're wrestling with and have a little humility or, a lot."

Tiger was arrested on suspicion of a DUI on March 27 after he rolled his car in an attempt to overtake a truck.

Authorities reportedly noted that he showed some signs of impairment and was lethargic, and they allegedly found two opioid pills in his pocket.

The father of two was charged with driving under the influence and refusal to submit to a urine test, and pleaded not guilty to the charges. He will appear in court on September 8 in relation to the case.

Tiger announced that he was stepping back from public life after the incident, in a statement posted to X that read: "I know and understand the seriousness of the situation I find myself in today. I am stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health. This is necessary in order for me to prioritize my well-being and work toward lasting recovery."

"I've committed to taking the time needed to return in a healthier, stronger, and more focused place, both personally and professionally," he continued.

"I appreciate your understanding and support, and ask for privacy for my family, loved ones and myself at this time."

Tiger then spent time at a rehab facility in Switzerland and returned in June, and has since flown under the radar.

articles.title: 'Mini-Rodri' Gonzalez shown he will be loved at Newcastle
articles.summary: Nico Gonzalez is given a rapturous welcome before Newcastle's Carabao Cup win against West Brom following the £52m midfielder's arrival from Manchester City.
articles.body:
Nico Gonzalez wanted to feel loved. He quickly got his wish at St James' Park on Wednesday night after completing his £52m move from Manchester City .

Newcastle United 's new signing was handed a rapturous welcome before he even kicked a ball for the club as supporters repeatedly chanted his name.

The sight of Gonzalez walking out at the sold-out stadium before the 3-2 win against West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup second round was a welcome one for head coach Matthias Jaissle, who desperately wanted him.

The German stressed he was "always a believer in the positive things", but tellingly also referred to the pursuit as a "long fight".

Having spoken personally to Gonzalez on a number of occasions, Jaissle made it clear how much he wanted the 24-year-old and how pivotal he would be in his side.

"It's always important if you're making signings like Nico that there is a commitment there," Jaissle said.

"But he showed that from the beginning, from our first conversations."

A lot has clearly changed since Gonzalez first set foot in the Premier League a year and a half ago and made his Manchester City debut against Newcastle. Of all teams.

Before City's 4-0 win, the new arrival had been warned about the intensity Newcastle's midfielders played and pressed with at their snarling best.

But the unfazed Spaniard ended up completing a staggering 100 passes, and helped snuff out any potential breakaways from the visitors at Etihad Stadium.

It was a glimpse of the skillset - in and out of possession - which convinced Manchester City to sign defensive midfielder Gonzalez from Porto for £50m.

City's then manager, Pep Guardiola, even labelled him "our mini-Rodri" in the absence of his influential, injured team-mate.

Gonzalez ultimately found an extended run of starts hard to come by once his compatriot returned to full fitness, though.

But former Manchester City assistant manager Kolo Toure believes he will have benefited from his experience at the Etihad.

"When you are in competition against players like Rodri, you learn a lot because you come up against them in training and you have to show the manager you are better than them," he said.

"You learn from things they do as well and, on the ball, he learned a lot from Rodri. Without the ball he's really good because he can press, get it back and read the game really well.

"He has this capacity to steal the ball from opponents, which is top. He's better than Rodri at this in my opinion, but Rodri on the ball is the best in the world.

"Both of them have different qualities and different strengths."

'He'll keep improving because of his mentality'

Gonzalez had a close relationship with Rodri and long humbly recognised that only a select number of players can start in his position at clubs bidding to challenge for the biggest honours.

Rodri was that man at Manchester City under Guardiola and, following the midfielder's move to Barcelona , new manager Enzo Maresca has signed Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille , having already brought in Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest .

The club also look set to make a bid for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez .

It was still not easy for Gonzalez to leave Manchester City, where he felt settled, but Newcastle will give him the platform he has been longing for as a key player.

The enthusiastic Spaniard sees this as an opportunity to develop further, which has always been a driver.

"His mentality is top," Toure said. "I would review games individually with the players and every time I had my laptop and sat next to him, he was so open to learning.

"He wanted me to show him and I wanted to help him because he was demanding in that way.

"You want to have players like this because they want to see what they do well and not well, and are open to criticism.

"He's going to keep on improving because of his mentality."

Gonzalez certainly did so when he left Barcelona, where his professional career started, and has such experience to fall back on.

Having spent a decade at Barca , and risen through the ranks, Gonzalez ultimately had to depart to truly flourish elsewhere.

Following a successful loan spell at Valencia , he joined Porto on a permanent basis at the age of 21 before earning a move to Manchester City.

Former Barcelona B team-mate Roger Riera feels he has developed "another vision" as a result.

"Nico has seen different countries and different styles of football," he said. "He's added a lot of things to his game, which have made him a more complete player.

articles.title: Bills should look to sign this former Chargers blocker
articles.summary: This veteran guard is suddenly available, and the Bills should be interested
articles.body:
If the Bills want to upgrade the guard and, especially, tackle depth on their roster, I have just the blocker for them.

Jamaree Salyer , formerly of Chargers and most recently of the Dolphins.

Right now, the presumed swing tackle on the Bills roster is third-year pro Tylan Grable , who only has 146 regular-season snaps on his professional resume to date, and the overwhelming majority of those reps have come in Week 18 the past two seasons.

He dealt with an injury in camp that forced him to miss the preseason opener, and while he did get back onto the field a week ago in Cleveland , Grable hardly looked up to the task of successfully blocking Browns outside rushers in the preseason. Swing tackles across the league aren't starters for a reason, yet the Bills can't feel incredibly confident in Grable's ability if he'd be needed to play this season. There's plenty of uncertainty with the former sixth-round pick at this stage of his development.

Like Grable, Salyer was a sixth-round pick, and a few days into free agency this past March, he signed a one-year deal in Miami but was placed on injured reserve with a knee injury on August 16.

Counting the playoffs, Salyer has 67 games of NFL experience under his belt.

He's a uniquely built blocker listed at 6'4" and 325 pounds — although he was 6'3" at the 2022 NFL Combine — therefore his frame is more of a prototypical guard than tackle. I vividly remember scouting Salyer ahead of the 2022 NFL Draft, he was a collegiate tackle who everyone — including myself — believed was best-suited at guard at the next level.

However, the Chargers essentially had no choice but to place Salyer at left tackle early in his rookie season after Rashawn Slater was lost for the season in Week 3. And Salyer thrived in his debut NFL campaign at left tackle protecting the blindside of Justin Herbert from Week 4 onward, including Los Angeles ' wild-card game against the Jaguars.

Altogether, Salyer logged 1,029 snaps that rookie season and was a pleasant surprise, particularly in pass protection. While the only game in which he did not allow a pressure was his first, in Week 4, Salyer surrendered more than five pressures in just one contest.

In 2023, Salyer played the entire season in Los Angeles at right guard, which totaled 1,144 snaps but lost his starting status ahead of the 2024 campaign but got on the field at left tackle, right tackle, and right guard.

A season ago, Salyer saw 509 snaps of game action for the Chargers at those three positions and allowed a career-low 22 pressures.

Lastly, there's familiarity with Salyer from a few current Bills players. He blocked alongside Sedrick Van Pran-Granger and paved lanes for James Cook at Georgia.

We aren't sure how healthy Salyer is now or when his knee will be back to 100%. But if the Bills are searching for more stable depth at tackle and guard ahead of the beginning of the regular season, Salyer should strongly considered.

articles.title: Fearnley among Britons closing in on US Open place
articles.summary: Jacob Fearnley is among the British players who stand one win away from a place in the US Open main draw in New York.
articles.body:
Britons Jacob Fearnley, Toby Samuel, Harry Wendelken and Harriet Dart stand one win away from a place in the US Open main draw after coming through their second round qualifying matches in New York.

Fearnley showed great resilience in battling to a three-set victory over Frenchman Luka Pavlovic, which set up a meeting with Austria's Jurij Rodionov.

The 25-year-old world number 100 recovered from a break of serve down to take the opening set, and held his nerve in the decider after his opponent levelled the match to clinch a 6-4 6-7 (4-7) 6-4 win.

Samuel, bidding to qualify for the US Open for the first time, produced a comeback victory against fellow Briton Billy Harris.

The 23-year-old, who made his slam debut at this year's French Open, recovered to win 4-6 6-4 6-1 and set up a meeting with Chile's former top-20 player Cristian Garin.

Wendelken, who has never contested the main draw at an overseas slam, saved a match point to come through a three-hour tussle with Switzerland's Remy Bertola.

The 24-year-old, ranked 196th, appeared on the brink of elimination at a set and 5-2 down, but denied Bertola a match point to level at 5-5 before edging the second-set tie-break.

Wendelken took charge of the decider, establishing a 5-2 lead, but was forced to withstand a late fightback from his opponent before eventually clinching a 5-7 7-6 (7-4) 6-4 win. He will face Lithuania's Vilius Gaubas next.

Dart also had to come from behind to maintain her bid in the women's draw.

The 77th-ranked Dart, 30, dominated the final two sets against American 16-year-old Kristina Penickova to progress 5-7 6-0 6-3 and could meet fellow Briton Heather Watson or Spain's Angela Fita Boluda.

Fran Jones, up against Germany's Mona Barthel, and Katie Swan, taking on American Mary Stoiana, will also aim to reach the third and final qualifying round on Wednesday.

However, Jack Pinnington Jones took the opening set but eventually fell to a 2-6 7-6 (8-6) 6-3 defeat by Finland's Otto Virtanen.

Former semi-finalist Grigor Dimitrov will face Virtanen after the 35-year-old maintained his bid for a 15th appearance in the US Open men's singles draw with a 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 win against Kazakhstan's Timofey Skatov.

China's two-time US Open quarter-finalist Zheng Qinwen, contesting a Grand Slam qualifying event for the first time since the 2022 Australian Open, won 6-1 7-5 against France's Clara Burel to set up a match against Russian Elena Pridankina.

There was also victory for 2019 US Open champion Bianca Andreescu, who defeated Ukraine's Veronika Podre 6-0 6-3.

The 26-year-old will have to find a way past Slovenia's 2021 French Open semi-finalist Tamara Zidansek to secure a first US Open main draw appearance in two years.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy applauds TaylorMade's Qi4D driver decision
articles.summary: At the Tour Championship, Rory McIlroy explained why he and other pros are excited about TaylorMade moving to a two-year driver cycle.
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy has a driver he likes and he's looking forward to playing it for the foreseeable future.

And why is this significant? Glad you asked.

In May, McIlroy's equipment sponsor, TaylorMade, announced it was moving to a two-year product cycle for its metal woods starting with the Qi4D family released last January. With the move, TaylorMade became the fourth of the six largest OEMs in the sport to move its metalwoods to a two-year product cycle, joining Ping, Srixon and Titleist. As of now, Callaway and Cobra have yet to share any intentions of moving off a yearly release cadence for their drivers.

"I think being able to use the same driver for say like an 18-month period I think just gives guys a little bit more of a level of comfort," McIlroy said Tuesday at the Tour Championship.

McIlroy, who said the move was a popular one among TaylorMade staffers, has a bit of a unique perspective on the situation given his struggles in recent years to move into new drivers. This season, with the Qi4D driver he switched into during its first week of availability in November, McIlroy is again among the top drivers on the PGA Tour , ranking second in Strokes Gained: Off the Tee. (That's despite, at times, complaining about his driver swing.)

He is averaging a career-high 330 yards in distance and his accuracy is more than three points higher than in 2024.

But just a season ago, McIlroy continued to use a TaylorMade Qi10 model from 2024 instead of 2025's Qi35. Fellow TaylorMade stablemate Scottie Scheffler also continued using the Qi10 up until two weeks ago, when he seemingly switched to the Qi4D for good during his win at the FedEx St. Jude Championship.

SHAPED FOR SPEED The re-engineered head profile increases ball speed thanks to improved aerodynamics developed through advanced simulations. FACE FOR DISTANCE 60x Carbon Twist Face™ is a technological cornerstone that provides weight savings, incredible ball speed and more consistency vs. a titanium face. ADJUSTABLE PERFORMANCE 4° loft sleeve can be used to adjust loft, lie and face angle for optimized flight. TOUR PROVEN TECHNOLOGIES New and improved cut-through Speed Pocket™ protects ball speed and reduces spin on low-face strikes. Advanced CAD modeling creates a design with a clean and powerful sound, a foundation of TaylorMade driver performance. Multi-Material Construction allows engineers to strategically place mass in areas of the head where it maximizes performance, speed, and stability.

ALSO AVAILABLE AT: PGA TOUR Superstore , TaylorMade

With TaylorMade not releasing a driver in 2027, Scheffler and McIlroy will head into the offseason knowing they won't even have to consider finding a new driver . Pros are never forced to switch to a new driver, but they usually will see some performance gain from year to year that motivates them.

However, they won't make a move at the expense of comfort, and the longer they use a driver, the more comfortable they get.

"You think about you really like a driver you're playing, and then something else is put in your hand say in October, November time, so nine or 10 months after you get your driver — all the manufacturers do a great job of fitting you into what is the best product for you, but they're all slightly different," McIlroy explained. "Thankfully I found a really good one that I like at the minute, but we call them snowflakes. Like one Qi4D with the same head, the same loft, same weighting. I'm on the exact same, to me sometimes just doesn't feel quite the same. It could be me, it could be a mental thing that I have."

McIlroy also pointed out that pros are often only able to use a driver for 18 months before it wears out and potentially becomes non-conforming. He and Scheffler both had their Qi10s fail USGA conformance tests at the PGA Championship last season and had to use backups.

"The heads go. I've obviously fallen foul of that at the PGA last year, Scottie as well," he said. "You really can only play a driver for a year to a year and a half before you've got to switch it out anyway."

Now with the two-year product cycle, McIlroy will just be starting the fitting process for a new driver by the time his gamer starts getting close to worn out.

articles.title: Merrill, Vásquez lead the Padres to a 3-0 victory over the Pirates
articles.summary: Jackson Merrill doubled, tripled, drove in a run and scored another to help Randy Vásquez reach 10 victories as the San Diego Padres beat the Pittsburgh Pira...
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Jackson Merrill doubled, tripled, drove in a run and scored another to help Randy Vásquez reach 10 victories as the San Diego Padres beat the Pittsburgh Pirates 3-0 on Wednesday to avoid a three-game sweep.

The Padres remained in possession of the National League's third wild-card spot, one game ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks . San Diego has won 12 of 17 and 22 of 31.

Merrill doubled to right with one out in the second off Bubba Chandler and scored on Luis Rengifo 's single to right.

Manny Machado reached on third baseman Nick Gonzales ' throwing error with one out in the fourth and came around on Merrill's triple to the right-field wall, sliding in headfirst and dragging his left hand across the plate.

Jake Cronenworth hit an RBI double in the eighth. Merrill drew an 11-pitch walk with two outs to load the bases before Jase Bowen flied out.

Vásquez retired his first nine batters before loading the bases with two outs in the fourth. He struck out Nick Gonzales to end it after catcher Freddy Fermin challenged a ball call that was overturned by the ABS system.

The right-hander held the Pirates to one hit in five innings, with two strikeouts and two walks. He has four wins and a no-decision in his last five starts. His previous high for victories in a season was six in 2025.

Griffin Canning got out of a bases-loaded jam in the seventh.

Bradgley Rodriguez pitched the final two innings for his second save. It was San Diego's 10th shutout.

The Pirates stranded 10 runners and were 1 for 13 with runners in scoring position.

Chandler (6-9) allowed two runs, one earned, and four hits in 5 2/3 innings. He struck out three and walked two.

Pirates RHP Jared Jones (2-5, 4.76 ERA) is scheduled to start Friday night in the opener of a three-game series at St. Louis .

The Padres haven't announced starter for the opener of a three-game series Friday night at Tampa Bay.

articles.title: Bob Myers explains how Sixers were able to land Jaylen Brown in a deal
articles.summary: Bob Myers explains how the Philadelphia 76ers were able to land Jaylen Brown in a deal from the Boston Celtics.
articles.body:
The first domino of the offseason for the Philadelphia 76ers was the big trade acquisition of Jaylen Brown from the rival Boston Celtics . The Sixers somehow pulled off a deal with the Cs to acquire Brown and that set up the big addition of LeBron James .

Brown brings a championship pedigree to Philadelphia as he won finals MVP for Boston's title team in 2024 and will be looking to bring his elite play to the Sixers. He averaged 28.7 points in a brilliant 2025-26 season and will be part of a big offensive game plan for a Philadelphia team looking to finally get over the hump in the Eastern Conference.

Bob Myers, President of Sports for HBSE and part of Philadelphia's front office, explained how the Sixers were able to land Brown while on an episode of "Cousins with Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady":

Jaylen Brown was not like we lost the Knicks and we're going to go get Jaylen Brown. Like, that's not what happened. That's not what happened. Then you start hearing there was a possibility, and the job then became is this a real thing with Jaylen Brown? Is it a real thing? I think Brad Stevens is one of the most straight shooters in the league. So, when you work in the NBA as an executive, you ultimately usually have at least one or two--I don't want to say transactions--with every other GM. So, you know, if I call Trace, 'Hey, you want to make a deal?' He might be like, 'Yeah, yeah, yeah.' And then he doesn't I mean, it's like--I know you're not this way--but you have to understand like he's honest or he might tell me what I want to hear or he might lie to me. This dude just might lie. He lied to me two years ago. He's going to lie to me again. That's not Brad Stevens. So, when Brad Stevens responded with, 'What are you offering?' Then you knew that there was a shot. So, then it becomes 50 conversations towards one, both organizations did a great job not leaking that, which is impossible. It's literally impossible, and by the way, having been in a job where we had high-profile players in Golden State , Brad ultimately and that organization are very sensitive to rumors around a guy like Jaylen Brown. So, I think they appreciated like 'Be quiet. Don't talk about this.' Which we didn't and they didn't. And so, it ended up just day-by-day getting legs.

The Sixers will be looking for Brown to give the Sixers that elite two-way ability and help Philadelphia in big moments, as he did with the Celtics during his 10 years in the league. It's a huge moment for the Sixers, which then set up the James signing. It was a home run for Myers and Co. in the City of Brotherly Love.

articles.title: 'He's human': Mason Miller gave up his first home run in over a year
articles.summary: One of baseball's most unreal streaks came to an end on Tuesday night at Petco Park.
articles.body:
Mason Miller 's unreal homerless streak came to an end in the top of the ninth inning at Petco Park on Tuesday night via a go-ahead solo shot from Oneil Cruz , the only run of the game in the San Diego Padres ' 1-0 loss to the Pittsburgh Pirates . Up until then, Miller hadn't given up a home run in over a calendar year.

After the game, Padres manager Craig Stammen summed up the rare misstep from baseball's most dominant closer in a few words.

"He's human," Stammen told reporters. "Part of the gig when you're pitching. Every once in a while, someone's gonna get you."

Or, as Miller put it when his manager's comments were relayed to him, "Humans can be idiots sometimes."

"Tip your hat," Miller told reporters. "Good swing. Crushed it obviously. But I just can't be throwing that pitch in that spot."

The pitch, a changeup, was perhaps just as rare a sighting from Miller as the long ball. It's the third pitch in his repertoire, but his fastball and slider are both so effective that he only throws it 2% of the time this season, according to Baseball Savant. And of that 2%, he's thrown the changeup exclusively to left-handed batters.

Miller felt good about his pitch selection, which he says was part of his plan from the scouting reports and prep work he had done leading up to the series against the Pirates. He tried to place it low and away but, instead, left it hanging over the inside part of the plate; a disastrous location against lefties, especially those with as much pop as Cruz.

The result was predictable: a 111.8 mph missile over the porch in right field.

"Looking back, I can be a good enough self-evaluator to say that that was a stupid pitch," Miller said. "But, yeah, I was convicted in it and had a plan. Didn't execute it."

Miller's status was unclear throughout most of Tuesday, as he had thrown 30 pitches in Monday's 12-inning loss to the Pirates and pitched in three of their last four games. But Miller said that didn't factor in. He went through his normal pregame routine and let Stammen know he was ready if he needed to be called upon.

"I felt good enough to go today," Miller said. "We had a lot of guys throw yesterday. That's part of my value and part of my responsibility to this team and to my teammates − to be available any time that I can.

"My workload's been high. But it wasn't: 'Yeah, I wasn't feeling good, didn't have my best stuff.' I think it was just one dumb pitch, and that's kind of the story."

Stammen, meanwhile, wasn't going to be one to question his shut-down closer in that situation.

"When a pitcher like Mason says 'Hey, give me the ball,' you're willing and able to give him the ball," Stammen said. "Especially where we're at in the season."

The Padres, one of the hottest teams in baseball over the past month, entered Wednesday just a half-game ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks for the third and final wild card spot in the National League.

articles.title: Tiger Woods makes rare appearance following DUI rehab stint
articles.summary: Legendary golfer Tiger Woods has returned to the public eye ahead of his DUI court appearance in September.
articles.body:
Since his DUI arrest in March, golf legend Tiger Woods has largely remained out of the public spotlight. He was involved in a rollover crash in South Florida while allegedly driving under the influence , with opioid tablets in his pocket after the crash.

Woods went to rehab in Switzerland following his arrest, before returning in May.

The 50-year-old Woods has rarely been seen since returning to the United States, but this week he made an appearance in a pre-recorded video for former pro golfer Notah Begay during the Payne Stewart Award ceremony.

Once the video surfaced online thanks to the Golf Channel , some fans expressed concern about his appearance, while others were happy to see the icon back in the spotlight. One user wrote, " Tiger looks a shell of his former self sadly ," while another, "He looks normal. Off the steroids and painkillers hopefully ."

Tiger Woods Records Video Message For Notah Begay

"Hey, Notah. It's been an unbelievable ride with you. You first came into my life when I was 11-years-old, playing in the Junior World, and you came to watch me play. Our friendship started there and never ended," Woods said in the video message. "To see what you've done off the golf course — I know you've won four times on the tour, playing in the Presidents Cup … but to see what you've done off the course and for your local Native American communities, you've helped over 80,000 youths and their families, which is absolutely incredible. What an amazing job at the sports complex in San Felipe.

"You've done an amazing job. I just think more people need to know what you've done and how you've served, and you've given back to the tribal lands and what you have done. There are so many people out there who are struggling in those communities, and you're trying to raise the bar to allow them to go on and achieve a lot more in life and have the successes that I think they deserve and you feel they deserve. Again, thank you for coming to see me play. Thank you for getting our friendship started, and I love you, dude."

While Woods has managed to stay out of the spotlight, he will be in court on September 8, when he makes his first court appearance in connection with the Florida crash.

articles.title: Minor League roundup, August 25: Dalton Wentz with a grand introduction
articles.summary: Yesterday on the farm.
articles.body:
For the final time this year, five of the San Francisco Giants Minor League Baseball affiliates were in action on Tuesday. Let's jump straight into it.

All listed positions in the roundup are the position played in that particular game.

A trio of pitchers are headed to AAA Sacramento from AA Richmond: RHPs Trystan Vrieling , R.J. Dabovich, and Darien Smith.

In less happy news, High-A Eugene RHP Ramon Marquez was placed on the 7-Day IL. Fingers crossed that it's nothing bad. Richmond shortstop Gavin Kilen (No. 7 CPL) was also placed on the IL, while Low-A San Jose RHP Sam Knowlton was released.

Sacramento River Cats beat the Reno Aces (D-Backs) 12-3 Box score

The Giants have a lot of outfielders, and it's going to create a thorny situation this offseason. Even having traded Heliot Ramos , San Francisco has 7 outfielders on the 40-man roster, and that doesn't even count Casey Schmitt , who might have pole position for the opening day left field spot.

That number figures to grow in the offseason, too. Bo Davidson (No. 4 CPL) will need to be protected from the Rule 5 Draft and, if he doesn't debut before then, it sure looks like Scott Bandura will need to be as well.

Bandura, a 7th-round pick in 2023, continued his assault on the league on Tuesday, hitting a nearly-perfect 4-5 with a triple, a walk, a stolen base, and 4 runs batted in.

On the one hand, that's an absurd day. On the other hand, it's kind of just the norm with Bandura these days. It was the 12th time this month that he's had a multi-hit game. It was the 4th game in a row in which he had multiple hits and at least 1 extra-base knock. It gave him a 6-game hitting streak, during which time he's gone 16-27 with 6 extra-base hits, 2 walks, and 0 strikeouts. It's given him a 2nd consecutive month with an OPS that begins with a 1.

Let's run the splits once more on his run in AAA following an early-season promotion:

First 34 games: 31-129, 1 home run, 2 triples, 7 doubles, 8 walks, 28 strikeouts Next 45 games: 71-181, 7 home runs, 1 triple, 14 doubles, 31 walks, 25 strikeouts

That all adds up to an .896 OPS and a 135 wRC+. Add in the 21 stolen bases (in just 22 attempts) and the solid defense, and that's a player who will absolutely need to be protected from the Rule 5 Draft … and possibly should be playing ahead of some of the other players on the MLB roster right now. The Giants have already had 4 outfielders make their Major League debuts this season … could that number soon be 5? It sure feels like the lefty has mastered the level.

Were he Rule 5 eligible, we might also be talking about an upcoming debut for third baseman Parks Harber (No. 17 CPL), who has seamlessly handled the transition to AAA. Unlike Davidson and Bandura, who had slow starts and then caught absolute fire, Harber has been more steady, for better and for worse. He's been extremely solid his entire time in AAA, without ever really struggling too much or going on an absolute heater. There's a lot to be said for consistency when that consistency is well above average!

Harber had himself a lovely Tuesday, hitting 3-4 with a double, a sacrifice fly, a walk, and a strikeout. He's now at an .894 OPS and a 133 wRC+ with Sacramento, and through 32 games he's really been a remarkably balanced offensive package. He's hitting for average (.313), hitting for power (.180 iso), drawing walks (11.8% rate), and limiting strikeouts (21.7% rate). With him not being Rule 5 eligible and an impending lockout, I'd guess that he stays in Sacramento for the rest of the year.

As for Davidson, he had a very rare hitless day, going 0-4 with a strikeout, but he did draw 2 walks.

Designated hitter Eddys Leonard had an awesome day, hitting 2-2 with a double and 3 walks. He's no longer on the 40-man roster, so we probably won't see him back in the Majors, but good to see him putting up nice numbers.

A fairly nondescript pitching performance in a bullpen game. The exciting news was that MLB LHP Matt Gage made his 2nd rehab appearance, and retired all 3 batters he faced, with a strikeout. The fact that Gage has returned to the mound this season at all is a big win, and it looks like we'll see him back in the Majors soon, too.

RHP Christian Alvarado got stretched to 3 innings of relief and handled them brilliantly, giving up 2 hits, 0 walks, and 0 runs, with 2 strikeouts. The 31-year old has been an excellent story and is settling in to his 1st AAA experience. He could be a factor in the MLB bullpen in 2027.

Richmond Flying Squirrels beat the Portland Sea Dogs (Red Sox) 8-7 Box score

The home run surge continues for first baseman Sabin Ceballos (No. 43 CPL). The just-turned 24-year old, who was a 3rd-round pick by the Braves in 2023 before being shipped to San Francisco in the Jorge Soler deal, went 1-3 in this game, with a walk, a stolen base, a strikeout, and, critically, a solo home run.

A year after Ceballos saw his power shockingly evaporate, the Oregon Duck has tapped back into it in a big way. Last year, Ceballos spent the entire season with Richmond and hit just 6 home runs. This year? He's already at 16 , despite only having 27 more plate appearances.

That power surge is exciting and encouraging but, unfortunately, it's not really leading to a good overall line, even though the righty draws a ton of walks, too. He has just a .741 OPS on the year which, thanks to the Eastern League's improved offense this year, is good for just a 104 wRC+, only 2 points over last season's. Ceballos continues to run an extremely bizarre low-strikeout, low-average profile. Despite striking out just 18.8% of the time, he has a meager .220 batting average, and those numbers were similar last year (17.4% and .232, respectively). That strikeout rate is 21st out of 121 EL hitters with at least 200 plate appearances this year … but the batting average is 95th. Very odd.

Richmond is currently lacking in top prospects, since outfielder Dakota Jordan (No. 5 CPL) and shortstop Gavin Kilen (No. 7 CPL) are both on the IL. So it was up to center fielder Trevor Cohen (No. 15 CPL) to hold it down for the big namers, and hold it down he did. Cohen, last year's 3rd-round pick, reached base in all 4 of his plate appearances, as he bopped 2 singles and drew 2 walks.

Cohen has been scuffling a bit following a hot start to AA. Over his last 12 games, he's 9-49 with no home runs, 1 triple, 1 double, 7 walks, and 7 strikeouts. It's still been a very strong debut at the level, given that this is his 1st full season of pro ball, and that he's playing excellent outfield defense with 14 stolen bases in 22 AA games. He has a .735 OPS and a 98 wRC+, though those numbers will likely come up given his 118 wRC+ with High-A Eugene.

Fairly uninteresting pitching performance. RHP Trystan Vrieling had another fine-but-not-particularly-good start, as he gave up 2 baserunners per inning, allowing 7 hits (including a home run), 3 walks, and 2 runs in 5 innings, with 5 strikeouts. That's just kind of been the year for Vrieling, who has been consistently mediocre. In 23 starts this year, the 2022 3rd-rounder (by the Yankees), Vrieling has given up 4 or more earned runs just 5 times, but has a 4.23 ERA and a 5.03 FIP, with just 8.3 strikeouts per 9 innings and 5.3 walks. Just not a ton to be excited about, unfortunately.

Another scoreless outing from LHP Jack Choate (No. 37 CPL), who retired all 3 batters he faced. It was Choate's 3rd straight game without allowing a hit, and he's really been strong this year save for one awful game in early July. Walks are the big issue for the funky southpaw right now, as he's given up 5.9 per 9 innings. The 11.2 strikeouts, however, have helped lead to a 3.05 ERA and a 3.92 FIP.

Eugene Emeralds beat the Everett AquaSox (Mariners) 10-4 Box score

There were two big stories from two exciting young talents, one on each side of the ball.

In the batter's box it was second baseman Dalton Wentz, who left the yard for the first time in his young career. Not only that, but he did it in grand fashion … the switch-hitter went 1-3 with 2 walks and a strikeout on the day, and smashed a glorious grand slam in the 1st inning.

Needless to say, that's a swing that Wentz will never, ever forget! It's been a slightly slow start for Wentz, which is understandable given that he went straight from college to High-A, with a few months in there to accumulate some rust. The 16th-rounder, who was given a 4th-round sized bonus, is 6-21 through 5 career games, with 2 extra-base hits, 2 walks, and 7 strikeouts. There's a lot in his bat worth being excited about, though, as that swing is evidence of!

The other excitement came on the mound, courtesy of LHP Jacob Bresnahan (No. 11 CPL). It was one of Bresnahan's worst games in a while from a run suppression standpoint, as he gave up 4 earned runs. But that certainly doesn't tell the whole story, as the 21-year old southpaw was otherwise dominant, giving up less than a baserunner per inning (4 hits and 1 walk in 6 frames) while striking out 10 batters. 10!

It was a doubly encouraging start because of how well Bresnahan settled into place. He let the 1st 3 baserunners he faced reach base, and then gave up a 1-out grand slam. And then that was that. He faced 15 more batters and retired 14 of them. He couldn't be touched.

The grand slam allowed was notable, however, and not just because it put runs on Bresnahan's sterling ERA, which sits at 2.92 (his FIP is lagging at 4.28). Bresnahan gave up just 2 home runs last year in Low-A, in 93 innings. This year? He's at 13 already, in just 98.2 frames.

But the good news? Those home runs are really the only bad news. Bresnahan is striking out 10.8 batters per 9 innings, only walking 3.5, and, perhaps most impressively, allowing opponents to hit just .183 against. That's the 2nd year running that Bresnahan is keep opposing hitters on the interstate! Mighty impressive.

Those were the stars, but there were some other nice performances. Left fielder Walker Martin went 3-4 with a walk, 2 stolen bases, and a strikeout; the 22-year old lefty has a .739 OPS, a 93 wRC+, and 18 stolen bases in 21 attempts. Shortstop Jhonny Level (No. 3 CPL) went 2-5 with a stolen base, a caught stealing, and a strikeout; the 19-year old switch-hitter is rocking an .867 OPS and a 128 wRC+, with 13 stolen bases in 19 attempts. And third baseman Hayden Jatczak hit 2-4 with a walk, a stolen base, 3 runs batted in, and an error; the 25-year old righty has a .685 OPS and an 88 wRC+ through 25 games at the level, with 3 stolen bases in as many attempts.

San Jose Giants beat the Visalia Rawhide (D-Backs) 6-5 Box score

An exciting game for the Baby Giants, who used a 4-run rally in the bottom of the 9th to turn a 5-2 deficit into a walk-off win. It was certainly a case of letting the other team grant you a gift, as the inning featured a walk, a hit batter, and 3 wild pitchers … the final of which allowed center fielder Peyton Bonds to score the go-home-happy run.

While it was a tremendously exciting end to the game, it wasn't a very exciting game from an individual performance standpoint. The offense was mild-mannered, with no extra-base knocks on the day. Bonds had another multi-hit game, though, as he went 2-5 with a strikeout and 2 runs batted in. Barry's nephew, taken in the 3rd round in July's draft, went 0-4 in his pro debut, but has gone 2-5 in both games since. A slower transition for second baseman Luke Nixon, the team's 5th-round pick, who went 1-4 with a strikeout and his 1st career stolen base. Nixon is 1-10 with 3 walks and 5 strikeouts, but hey, he's got an average now!

Another really nice game for left fielder Broedy Poppell, who went 2-3 with a walk, a strikeout, and a stolen base. It's been a tough season for last year's 13th-rounder, but he's been red hot lately: in his last 7 games, Poppell has hit 12-23 with 7 extra-base hits and 7 walks, bringing his OPS up to .782 and his wRC+ to 100, with 15 stolen bases in as many attempts (impressive success rate!). Right fielder Tanner Mally, July's 17th-round pick, continues to look comfortable, as he went 1-3 with 1 walk, 2 hit by pitches, 2 stolen bases, and a strikeout. Through 15 games, Mally has a .972 OPS, a 158 wRC+, and 4 stolen bases in as many attempts.

RHP Trey Seeley had a pretty strong day on the mound, cruising through 6 innings while allowing just 3 hits, 1 walk, and 2 runs, with 5 strikeouts, though he gave up a home run. A 14th-round pick out of Hope International a year ago, Seeley has been pretty strong lately, after a slow start to his career. But, despite that, one of the funnier stats in the system took a step forward with this game, as Seeley did a good job limiting hits, but did give up a home run. That has been the season for him, and the numbers are truly shocking: Seeley has given up 42 hits this year with the Baby Giants, and 14 of them have left the park. Add in the home run he allowed in 9 innings in the Complex League, and Seeley has given up 15 big flies this year, which is 4th-most in the entire system. The 48.2 innings pitched? 40th. And that's how you end up with a 6.84 ERA and a 7.46 FIP across the 2 levels.

DSL Giants Black lost to the DSL Padres Gold 8-3 Box score

And with that, the DSL season is over. The Giants Orange team didn't make the playoffs and, after a nice run, the Giants Black team was eliminated.

It was not for lack of effort by their starting pitcher, RHP Santiago Guerrero. The 19-year old from Mexico capped off an intriguing debut season with a dominant showing, striking out 7 batters in 5 shutout innings, while allowing just 1 hit and 1 walk. What a spectacular game! You don't see pitching performances like that in the DSL very frequently.

Guerrero, who ended the regular season strong, finished the season (which doesn't include his pair of postseason starts) with a 3.34 ERA but a 6.04 FIP. Including the postseason, he struck out 49 batters in 43 innings … but walked 38. There was a lot to love, but a lot to work on in his 2nd season.

Right fielder Vinicius Dos Santos had a pinch hit home run, which was notable since it was just his 2nd career home run in 3 seasons. Center fielder Djean Macares went 2-4 with a walk and 2 stolen bases. The 18-year old from Aruba finished his 2nd season with an .828 OPS, a 121 wRC+, 26 stolen bases, and a 9.7% strikeout rate … my guess would be that this was his final game in the DSL.

articles.title: Three-time Pro Bowl defensive end Za'Darius Smith stepped away last year after losing three family members
articles.summary: Za'Darius Smith said he was in a dark place after losing his mother, grandmother, and father before signing with the Atlanta Falcons for 2025.
articles.body: Within months of abruptly stepping away from the NFL last season, Za'Darius Smith lost his mother, his grandmother, and his father in rapid succession. Now, after navigating unimaginable grief, the three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher is back on the field, using football as his sanctuary with the Atlanta Falcons. After playing for six different franchises across 11 seasons, the 33-year-old was ready to hang up his cleats when he left the Philadelphia Eagles mid-season in October 2025. FALCONS COACH KEVIN STEFANSKI MAY POACH FORMER PRO BOWL PASS RUSHER FROM BROWNS TEAM THAT FIRED HIM But when Atlanta came calling, Smith was navigating a heavy personal trial that ultimately brought him back to the game. Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Smith opened up about heartbreak, healing, and his return to the field. "I was in a dark place," Smith said. He visited with the Cleveland Browns before reaching a deal with Atlanta, his seventh NFL team, saying football served as a much-needed outlet during a brutal stretch. Smith’s signing gives Atlanta needed pass-rushing reinforcement following a season-ending ACL injury to Jalon Walker and an eight-game suspension for James Pearce Jr. FALCONS SELECTED TWO PASS RUSHERS IN NFL'S 2025 DRAFT AND NEITHER MIGHT BE AVAILABLE TO START 2026 "This is my happy place," Smith said. "Come back, play football. I was in a dark place, but, you know, coming out, running out on the field, the fans, not just the fans, man, the joy that I get from winning and just getting sacks." "My mom, rest her soul, man, she always wanted me to be in Atlanta with the Falcons." Since entering the league in 2015, the defensive end has put up consistently strong production, tallying 343 total tackles, 70.5 sacks, 16 pass deflections, 10 forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries. Smith will turn 34 near the start of the season. VON MILLER SIGNS WITH COWBOYS IN HOMECOMING MOVE FOR 2-TIME SUPER BOWL CHAMPION: 'LET'S MAKE THIS ONE SPECIAL' Speaking on his career sack count, Smith added: "Now I'm trying to reach 100. However I need to do that, I'm going to try." "I'm happy to be in Atlanta." articles.title: Northern Nigeria’s female basketball players chase bigger dreams
articles.summary: A grassroots basketball initiative is giving girls in northern Nigeria a chance to train, compete and dream bigger.
articles.body:
Abuja, Nigeria – Khamila Sani Ibrahim remembers growing up in Kano State in northern Nigeria, where opportunities for girls to play organised sport were limited and seeing girls on the basketball court was uncommon.

When visiting her grandparents during school holidays, she had to find ways to fit basketball around family expectations.

“It is very hard for me to train in basketball,” Ibrahim said. “I only go out to play when they are not around, or I tell them that I’m going to visit my friends, and from there I go to the court.”

Across northern Nigerian communities, sports such as basketball and football have historically been viewed as male-dominated spaces. For girls who want to play, the obstacles can include limited access to courts and equipment, a shortage of coaching and funding, and fewer chances to compete.

Now, through Grassroots To Greatness (G2G), an initiative dedicated to female empowerment in sports, girls are finding opportunities to train, compete and develop their skills.

Jawahir Bello, a youth sports advocate, founded the initiative after seeing how few opportunities were available to girls in the region.

At tournaments, players wear custom hijabs, long sports vests and athletic tights.

“Our core value is about participating in sports without doing anything that goes against our cultural values or our identity as Muslims,” Bello told Al Jazeera. “Whether you put on a hijab or innerwear under your jersey, modesty is key. You come out modest, decent and fully covered.”

Although she anticipated resistance from some communities when launching female-only tournaments and community training sessions, Bello said she has been encouraged by community stakeholders who have welcomed the initiative.

To mobilise participants, G2G partners directly with local grassroots coaches who already run community teams on the ground.

When Ibrahim represented Kano State in a multi-state G2G tournament featuring female players from up to nine different states, she found herself in an environment unlike the male-dominated local teams she had previously played with, where girls were often underestimated.

“What G2G did for us was incredible,” Ibrahim said. “They provided jerseys, custom hijabs, basketballs, cover for our transport and even financial stipends for all the teams, regardless of who won or lost. It made us feel seen and valued.”

Fatima Diouf, another young player based in Abuja, started playing basketball at her school when she was 11. She joined the G2G programme to test her skills against tougher competition. Though her team fell short of the finals, she left with lessons she says will stay with her.

“I have learned a lot beyond just basketball. I learned teamwork, confidence, discipline and how to keep improving,” Fatima told Al Jazeera.

For Ibrahim, getting time on the court is still not always easy. She has had to push past self-doubt and the dismissive attitude of male peers who assumed girls could not compete at the same level. She also struggles to balance intense training with domestic chores and schoolwork.

Mansur Abdullahi, assistant coach of Nigeria’s U-20 women’s national football team, the Falconets, says grassroots coaches and organisations can help create opportunities for young athletes that larger sports structures may not reach.

“Official sports bodies have big structures, but local groups provide the actual trust and cultural understanding,” he said. “So it’s only through community-led initiatives that more professional teams will understand what’s acceptable for girls and boys and how to frame sports so it fits the existing values instead of clashing with them.”

For many participants, the tournaments are a chance to test themselves against new opponents and think about what could come next.

Before joining G2G, Ibrahim’s father had reservations about whether competitive sports would compromise family standards. But once he attended her games and saw the athletic wear and the structured environment of the initiative, he became one of her biggest supporters.

“I want to secure a college sports scholarship in the United States and eventually turn professional. More than that, I want other Muslim girls across northern Nigeria to see that sports build your health, strength, and confidence, and that nothing should hold you back from chasing your dreams,” Ibrahim told Al Jazeera.

Seeing the network of coaches, stakeholders and organisers at the tournament also broadened Diouf’s perspective and allowed her to imagine playing across Africa.

For G2G, the ambition goes beyond organising female-only tournaments. Bello wants the programme to show girls there is a place for them in sport and that they can compete without feeling that they have to give up who they are.

“You can keep your identity, stay covered and still achieve something in life,” Bello said.

articles.title: Asian Games: Questions over selections across squads
articles.summary: More sports News: NEW DELHI: India's Asian Games squads are facing fresh selection scrutiny with questions being raised over the criteria used in gymnastics, kurash and.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Asian Games squads are facing fresh selection scrutiny with questions being raised over the criteria used in gymnastics, kurash and karate.In gymnastics, Pranati Nayak is the lone athlete to be cleared. There is no explanation on why other gymnasts who earned nominative, by-name quotas from the Asian Gymnastics Union (AGU) were not considered.Following the 2026 Asian Championships, Nishka Agarwal earned a nominative all-around qualification while Pranati and Protistha Samanta secured nominative qualification as vault specialists. The 2025 Asian meet adds context - Pranati won bronze while Protishta finished fourth.The 2026 championships, held after June 20, fell outside the ministry's qualification window. But if the 2025 Asian event was used as criteria, then Protishta, too, should have made the cut.Protishta had India's best gymnastics result at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, finishing seventh and becoming the only Indian gymnast to reach the final. Pranati competed there injured and could not make the final cut. "The question is whether the framework was applied consistently for the Asian Games. If yes, then on that basis, Protishta and Nishka, along with men's gymnasts Tapan Mohanty and Yogeshwar Singh, also deserved consideration," said federation sources.Kurash raises another question. India returned from the Hangzhou Games without a medal, yet a six-member team has been cleared after an initial decision by authorities not to send one. With no performance benchmark cited, the selection remains unclear.Karate is equally perplexing. SAI had formed a committee and initially decided not to send a team, according to sources. Yet Alisha Choudhary and Chetan Bhatt have been named. articles.title: TCU football pulls credentials from local newspaper for reporting on locker room assault story
articles.summary: TCU athletics rescinded the Fort Worth Star-Telegram's media credentials days before the Horned Frogs face Bill Belichick's North Carolina team in Dublin.
articles.body: TCU Horned Frogs football has a chance to make a run in a wide open Big 12 Conference, coming off a 9-4 season in 2025. But if they do, local fans who subscribe to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram won't have access to the type of reporting they might normally expect. The Star-Telegram reported recently about an incident in the TCU locker room that resulted in senior safety Jacob Fields being dismissed from the football team. Fields allegedly assaulted another player, wide receiver Dozie Ezukanma, though the initial report didn't identify him directly. Ezukanma posted a now-deleted Instagram video acknowledging that he was the other player involved. TCU has now, per the paper, rescinded the Star-Telegram’s credentials to cover Horned Frogs athletics. And it's supposedly because of the "health and wellbeing" of student athletes. "Unfortunately, an unnamed source without first-hand knowledge of the incident provided inaccurate information cited in initial reporting by the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, which we strongly disputed. "The inclusion of the misinformation advanced a narrative that endangered a student-athlete and resulted in threats to him and his family. Banning news organizations from doing their jobs is not what schools and athletic departments should be doing. Given the player identified himself, how TCU is blaming this on the Star-Telegram is inexplicable. articles.title: Czech pair Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik win US Open mixed doubles
articles.summary: Duo secure first Grand Slam trophy as a team after defeating Switzerland’s Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli of Italy.
articles.body:
Czech pair Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik beat Switzerland’s Belinda Bencic and Italian Flavio Cobolli 6-3, 1-6, 10-6 to win the US Open mixed doubles title, securing their first Grand Slam trophy as a team.

Muchova and Mensik got off to a fast start in Arthur Ashe Stadium on Wednesday, with the hard-serving Mensik hammering an ace past Bencic on set point to claim the opener in less than 30 minutes.

Bencic drilled a return winner to break serve for a 3-1 lead in the second and the Swiss player later levelled the match when her forehand clipped the net cord and skipped beyond Muchova.

In the deciding 10-point match tiebreak, Mensik’s big serve and sharp work at the net helped the Czechs seize control.

The 20-year-old put away a firm volley to open an 8-4 lead before Muchova produced her best serve of the match to bring up championship points.

Mensik sealed the victory with another ace, leaping in celebration after clinching the first trophy of the season’s final Grand Slam.

Muchova and Mensik had earlier saved two match points against Russians Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev in their semifinal to book their place in the title match.

“I think in the end the matching outfits made the difference for us,” Muchova said during the trophy ceremony.

“I wasn’t really expecting to be standing here tonight. We came out just to have fun and enjoy these mixed doubles and now we are standing here. So we did something right.

“I think this is a really good start to the US Open for all of us,” she added after congratulating Bencic and Cobolli.

The 16-team mixed doubles draw began on Tuesday in the second year of the tournament’s revamped format, which features leading singles players and is aimed at drawing bigger crowds in the week before the singles main draw.

Among the star-studded teams, Novak Djokovic joined forces with Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz played alongside Serena Williams .

articles.title: Roberto Gómez: "Qué mala suerte tiene España con gente como Laporta"
articles.standfirst: El periodista carga en La Tribu contra el presidente del Barcelona por el frustrado homenaje a los campeones del mundo y también habla del Real Madrid y del futuro de Julián Álvarez
articles.summary: El periodista carga en La Tribu contra el presidente del Barcelona por el frustrado homenaje a los campeones del mundo y también habla del Real Madrid y del futuro de Julián Álvarez
articles.body: Roberto Gómez fue especialmente contundente en La Tribu, con Javi Amaro, al analizar la suspensión del homenaje a los campeones del mundo del Barcelona. El periodista lamentó que los internacionales azulgranas no puedan exhibir el trofeo ante su afición y señaló directamente al presidente culé: "Qué mala suerte tiene España. Y qué mala suerte tiene España con gente como Joan Laporta". Gómez mostró especialmente su pesar por los propios futbolistas del Barça. "Qué vergüenza, qué pena, qué lástima y qué dolor. Primero por los jugadores", aseguró. "De verdad que es, yo creo, lo más triste y lamentable que se ha visto en la historia del fútbol español", sentenció durante su intervención. El periodista insistió en sus críticas: "Que los jugadores del equipo campeón, y además con una representación de la que nos sentimos todos orgullosos, de los jugadores del Barcelona, no puedan exhibir y enseñar el trofeo, que es el más grande que van a conquistar en su vida, y todo con la anuencia del presidente del Barcelona. ¡Qué vergüenza!". "Para mí es un día triste", añadió antes de mostrar su "empatía total con los futbolistas" y con los aficionados del Barcelona. Gómez cerró su reflexión sobre este asunto insistiendo en Laporta: "Qué pena y qué mala suerte tiene España con algunos personajes como es el caso de Joan Laporta". Laporta también apareció en la conversación por el futuro de Julián Álvarez. Roberto Gómez fue muy crítico con la actuación del presidente azulgrana respecto al delantero rojiblanco: "Lo que está haciendo Laporta al Atlético de Madrid es un chantaje". Ante la pregunta directa de Javi Amaro sobre si Julián terminará marchándose al Arsenal, Gómez no dejó lugar a dudas: "Julián se queda en el Atlético de Madrid". El periodista también defendió al futbolista después de su ausencia en el entrenamiento y rechazó cuestionar los motivos ofrecidos: "Hay que creer en las personas. Los servicios médicos del Atlético de Madrid me parecen de los mejores del mundo, los creo". Roberto Gómez también valoró el partido del Real Madrid ante la Real Sociedad y se mostró satisfecho con el conjunto blanco: "Sí, me gustó, muy bien. La segunda parte fue muy buena". Entre los nombres propios, "me gustaría destacar sobre todo Bellingham. Me gustó muchísimo, más allá de los tres goles de Mbappé". También tuvo buenas palabras para Cucurella, Oyarzabal y la respuesta de la grada: "Muy bien el público del Bernabéu. Yo creo que es para ponerlo en todo lo alto". Por último, Roberto Gómez cargó contra la ausencia pública del presidente de la Federación: "Es impresentable la ausencia de Louzán, el presidente, que lleva un mes desaparecido. Vaya vacaciones que se está metiendo, con la que está cayendo en el fútbol español y no sabemos absolutamente nada de él, que ha comenzado LaLiga desaparecido".
