articles.title: ‘Ted Lasso’ discovers soccer’s clique problem, one that the USWNT has mastered
articles.summary: Spoiler alert: This article contains spoilers for this week’s episode of Ted Lasso Apple TV’s favorite soccer coach, Ted Lasso, has dealt with a lot over the...
articles.body:
Spoiler alert: This article contains spoilers for this week's episode of Ted Lasso

Apple TV's favorite soccer coach, Ted Lasso, has dealt with a lot over the previous three seasons: divorce, egos, bullying, relegation, panic attacks, promotion and Jamie Tartt.

But in the latest episode of season 4, AFC Richmond's women's team has introduced him to a new problem: cliques.

They are inevitable and, at their most extreme, they can tear a team apart.

As Dr. Sharon Fieldstone, Ted's fictional beloved psychologist, explains to former Richmond reporter Trent Crimm on his podcast, if coaches "lose the dressing room, they lose the team."

"Successful teams are happy teams, and happy teams have coaches that establish a culture of communication and trust," she says. "The majority of that happens in the dressing room."

Cliques are a reality of soccer, and they are considerably more complicated than "Ted Lasso" suggests. They exist on almost every team from youth to professional and even championship-winning teams like the 2015 and 2019 U.S. women's national teams.

"Even within our squad, the culture has changed," former U.S. forward Carli Lloyd said in an episode of Hope Solo 's now-defunct podcast recorded in 2022, a few months after her retirement as one of the team's all-time goalscorers. Lloyd and Solo were roommates and close friends during the 2015 World Cup.

"It was really tough and challenging to play these last several years. To be quite honest, I hated it. It wasn't fun going in. It was only for love of the game, really, for me. I wanted to win and wanted to help the team, but the culture within the team was the worst I had ever seen it."

Lloyd and Solo similarly considered themselves "black sheep" within the group.

Expecting 26 players to become best friends simply because they wear the same jersey is unrealistic. Every player enters a locker room with a different history, relationships, loyalties and different amounts of power.

A 16-year-old rookie midfielder might sit next to a 35-year-old defender at the end of her career. A player fighting for her next contract might share a locker with a national team star earning considerably more in salary and endorsements. International players arrive sometimes without speaking the language. Former college and youth teammates reconnect. Others may actively dislike each other after years spent as rivals.

According to a study published in The Sport Psychologist , based on interviews with 18 collegiate athletes across nine teams, athletes considered clique formation "inevitable." Age, tenure, proximity and similarity all helped determine which athletes gravitated toward one another.

So how do you stop a clique from destroying a team? As Dr. Fieldstone explains to Crimm: give them a common enemy. Suddenly, the divisions inside the locker room matter less, and the team can unite against something bigger than itself. Perhaps the best example of this comes from one of the most successful locker rooms in women's soccer history.

The U.S. teams that won back-to-back World Cup titles in 2015 and 2019 were full of enormous personalities, yet they found something more powerful than their competing celebrity. They got angry.

The 2015 World Cup victory was followed by one of the most consequential collective fights in the history of women's sports. The players turned their attention toward U.S. Soccer and what they viewed as systemic inequality in pay, travel, playing conditions and treatment.

In March 2016, Lloyd, Solo, Alex Morgan , Becky Sauerbrunn and Megan Rapinoe filed an Equal Employment Opportunity Commission complaint alleging wage discrimination against U.S. Soccer.

Sauerbrunn explained at the time that the entire team had agreed to the complaint. The five players had been elected by their teammates to represent them in collective bargaining and therefore became the names attached to the filing.

Players with different personalities, ideologies and levels of fame suddenly had a shared objective: equal pay. The fight was bigger than the cliques.

As the battle extended into the next generation, so did the collective nature of the team.

By the 2019 World Cup, Solo was no longer in goal, but many players from the 2015 squad remained. The fight with U.S. Soccer had escalated dramatically, with 28 USWNT players filing a gender-discrimination lawsuit just months before the tournament that they eventually won.

The U.S. women's national team is hardly the only team to discover that getting everyone pulling in the same direction is easier said than done; but done right it can be effective.

Arsenal and England captain Leah Williamson served as an authenticity consultant for "Ted Lasso's" fourth season, answering writers' questions about women's football throughout production. We can't say for certain which parts of the show she directly advised on. However, Williamson experienced both a club team that overcame reported locker room rifts when Arsenal won the UEFA Champions League and a national team that had plenty of outside noise heading into the 2025 European Championship.

Ahead of the 2025 Euros, England goalkeeper Mary Earps abruptly retired from international football and defender Millie Bright withdrew from selection due to mental and physical burnout. Neither was necessarily in coach Sarina Wiegman's starting line-up plans despite their successful legacy with the team. When giant personalities exit the locker room, it shakes up the dynamics. Still, the team found a way to overcome early tournament struggles to win a second European title. Wiegman's explanation for the success: "B****** get s*** done."

For the U.S., it was fighting for equal pay. For the Lionesses, it was silencing the doubters. For AFC Richmond women, it was trivia and a good old-fashioned pub fight against a group of misogynistic hecklers at the Crown & Anchor.

Because sometimes it's not about being friends. It's about getting s*** done.

articles.title: Nico Rosberg praises Nico Hulkenberg's "spectacular" Dutch GP save
articles.summary: Nico Hulkenberg narrowly avoided a high-speed collision with his Audi team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto at the Dutch Grand Prix
articles.body:
2016 Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg has lauded Nico Hulkenberg's "spectacular" reactions to avoid a high-speed collision with his Audi team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto during a chaotic opening lap of the Dutch Grand Prix.

While the rain had stopped before the start of the race, there were still some wet patches on the track. As Red Bull's Max Verstappen made his way around the banked final corner, he hit a damp spot and crashed into the barriers. Bortoleto suffered a similar incident but managed to continue after a 360-degree spin.

As his Audi team-mate spun in front of him, Hulkenberg found himself in a cloud of tyre smoke, and when it dissipated, he was met with Bortoleto in front of him.

Speaking during the Sky Sports F1 broadcast, Rosberg pointed out how the 39-year-old managed to avoid a big crash.

"It just shows how quick those drivers react. Hulkenberg went in; he knew more or less where Bortoleto was, where his trajectory was going," Rosberg explained. "He has a white wall, but then at the last moment sees him and bam, reacts and avoids [a crash].

"It was a spectacular reaction from Hulkenberg, so I don't think it was just luck. I think there was also some skill there to avoid that big crash."

Hulkenberg went on to claim his best result of the season with eighth place and four valuable points for Audi. Bortoleto successfully recovered from his spin to finish 13th.

The German driver described the near-miss while speaking to Sky Sports Germany: "Yeah, it was tricky and dicey. Naturally, I saw it all happen almost in slow motion at that speed.

"But Turn 14 was simply still completely wet and, on slicks, it's a bit of a thriller, of course. I saw him lose the car—like I said, slow motion and at speed. But then you don't know exactly whether he's going to slide up or slide down, what's going to happen.

"And it was clear to me: hey, I have to try to somehow get around this. On top of that, there was all the debris and the smoke from Max ahead. So it looked wild and spectacular. I slowed down and tried to wait as long as possible before deciding which way to go. A sheet of paper would have fitted between us, but not much more."

articles.title: Texas A&M WR makes Shaun Alexander Freshman of the Year Award List
articles.summary: Texas A&M freshman WR Aaron Gregory was named to the Shaun Alexander Freshman of the Year Award Watch List on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Texas A&M's loaded wide receiver room is led by junior Mario Craver , who finished second on the team with 59 receptions for 917 yards and 4 touchdowns during his first season with the Aggies, and will now serve as redshirt junior quarterback Marcel Reed's No. 1 receiver this fall.

Combined with Ashton Bethel-Roman, former five-star prospect Terry Bussey, and Alabama transfer Isaiah Horton, Marcel Reed should, at the very least, match his 2025 production after passing for a career-high 3,169 yards, 25 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions last season.

Through 16 preseason practices, Reed has connected with every receiver mentioned, while freshman WR Aaron Gregory, who shined during his first action this spring, has made new coach Mike Elko and OC Holmon Wiggins' jobs much harder ahead of releasing the first official depth chart before the Aggies host Missouri State in just nine days.

A former blue-chip prospect who, in my humble opinion, should have been a five-star recruit based on his size, speed, and advanced route running and separation, the Georgia native is ready to contribute as a reserve option who could see his first action during the season opener, likely serving as Isaiah Horton's primary backup as the X receiver.

On Wednesday, Gregory was named to the Shaun Alexander Freshman of the Year Award Watch List, and while his usage this season is still up in the air, from a talent perspective, Gregory is simply too good to keep off the field and will provide elite depth at one of the most important positions.

During his high school career at Douglas County, Gregory reeled in 163 receptions for 2,930 yards (18.0 average) and 20 touchdowns.

articles.body:
Manchester City attacker Jack Grealish has reportedly decided that he wants to join Everton ahead of Aston Villa if he leaves the Etihad Stadium club this summer. The Englishman spent last season on loan with the Toffees and Everton manager David Moyes wants him back at the Hill Dickinson Stadium club. However, Grealish also has an offer from former club Villa, with the Midlands club desperate to bolster their attack. Villans boss Unai Emery is set to be without Ollie Watkins and he wants reinforcements in the final third.

Villa wants Grealish back but the 30-year-old is keen on returning to Everton if he leaves Man City. He featured against Arsenal in the Community Shield and also came off the bench against Bournemouth in City's first Premier League game of 2026-27. Enzo Maresca could opt to hold on to the Toffees target but there are no guarantees that he will get to play regularly given the options available to the new City manager.

Grealish was a regular at Everton last season before an injury ended his loan spell, starting 18 of the 20 Premier League games he featured in.

articles.body:
Nottingham Forest have completed the signing of striker Liam Delap on a five-year deal for a reported package of £50 million.

Delap joins the club after a difficult first season at Chelsea , who he joined after impressing for Ipswich Town. Indeed, the striker played 47 times for the Blues across all competitions, scoring just three times.

However, Delap now has a chance to get back to his best form at Forest after signing until 2031.

"I really can't wait to get started, this is a massive club with a big history," the 23-year-old said on his arrival at the club.

"I spoke to the manager and I like his way, I think he can be the one to really help me develop and make that next step and hopefully I can bring goals here.

"I can't wait to hear the noise at the City Ground and have the fans on my side because I know how loud and important they are.

"As a team we can build something really strong and the main aim is to challenge and be a top club in the Premier League."

Delap could be in line for his Forest debut on Saturday as Oliver Glasner 's side face the difficult trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool .

articles.title: What is the Vikings biggest concern heading into 2026?
articles.summary: The biggest concern surrounding the 2026 Vikings may lie elsewhere besides the quarterback.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings ' quarterback situation has dominated headlines this offseason. Even after Kyler Murray was named the team's starter, speculation continues to swirl around J.J. McCarthy 's future with the team.

Murray himself has a lot to prove in 2026, having only played a full season once over the past four seasons. Uneven performances in the Vikings' joint practices against the Baltimore Ravens last week didn't exactly put concerns to rest.

However, Minnesota is expecting the rest of the roster to help elevate Murray. But what if those areas aren't sufficient, either?

Gordon McGuiness of PFF suggested the Vikings' pass rush, not their quarterback room, is the team's biggest concern as the 2026 season approaches .

The Vikings traded away edge defender Jonathan Greenard , who led the team with 47 total pressures last season. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores' scheme relies heavily on the blitz, so linebacker Eric Wilson could once again rank among the team's leaders in total pressures. That approach also reduces the need for a true difference-maker off the edge compared to many other defenses, but the lack of an edge defender with a PFF pass-rush grade above 75.0 does limit the unit's flexibility.

Christian Darrisaw was praising Dallas Turner earlier this week, saying the third-year EDGE rusher is primed for a " special " season. Turner was extremely disruptive during the joint practices against the Ravens.

However, until we see it in real games, it's going to be a tall task for Turner to replicate Greenard's production over the past two seasons. If Turner takes that step, Minnesota could once again terrorize quarterbacks. But if he doesn't translate his training camp success into regular season viability, the Vikings' pass rush could suffer, creating a domino effect throughout the rest of the defense.

articles.body:
NOTTINGHAM, England (AP) — Chelsea sold Liam Delap to Nottingham Forest on Thursday in a deal worth a reported 50 million pounds ($68 million) for a striker who scored two goals in all competitions last season.

Delap was only at Chelsea for one season and failed to establish himself as a regular after joining from Ipswich for 30 million pounds.

The 23-year-old Delap has signed a five-year deal at Forest, where he will provide competition for Igor Jesus and Chris Wood .

Delap was the top scorer with 12 goals for Ipswich in the 2024-25 season when the team was relegated from the Premier League. That earned him the move to Chelsea.

articles.summary: The Thai reflects on his road to ONE ahead of his clash against Lenny Blasi at The Inner Circle 28 on August 28.
articles.body:
Thai firecracker Worapon Lukjaoporongtom has quickly become one of the standout performers in ONE Championship's weekly series, and he now steps into the biggest opportunity of his career.

The 23-year-old headlines The Inner Circle 28 against Italian standout Lenny Blasi in a bantamweight Muay Thai main event on Friday, August 28, streaming exclusively for members at live.onefc.com in Asia primetime from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium.

He enters the bout riding an impressive three-fight winning streak through 2026, with a US$100,000 main roster contract now firmly within reach.

Before he chases that life-changing opportunity, here is a look back at the long road that carried him here.

Every fighter has an origin story, and Worapon's begins at home in Buriram, in a household where Muay Thai was never a question of if, only when.

His father, a devoted fan of the sport, made the decision early, enrolling his son in training well before the boy had any say in the matter himself. Looking back on those early days now, he still remembers how it all began.

"I started really young, around kindergarten, when I was about 6 years old. But, honestly, I didn't even like Muay Thai. My dad was a huge fight fan, while I preferred playing football."

That reluctance did not last. Worapon eventually gave the sport a shot, and what started as a spur-of-the-moment decision at a local temple festival ended up changing the course of his childhood.

Life growing up in rural Buriram came with its own modest realities, and the reward that came with that first battle meant more than just bragging rights among friends.

"My first fight happened when I was 7, and I had zero training beforehand. There was a local temple festival in our village, and I always saw them training and holding fights, so I wanted to give it a try. I just went up there throwing wild punches like any kid would. "Surprisingly, I won that first fight and earned about 150 Thai Baht (approximately US$4.50), which I used to buy a remote-controlled car I'd been eyeing. Earning my own money as a kid without having to ask my parents made me fall in love with it, and I wanted to keep fighting."

Every Muay Thai fighter chasing a career in Thailand dreams of competing on the country's most iconic stages, and Worapon's first shot at one came during his teenage years.

Stepping into that spotlight for the first time, however, was an entirely different experience from anything he had known.

"My first Bangkok fight was at Channel 7 Stadium, and I was incredibly nervous. I grew up watching Channel 7 Muay Thai on TV, so I never imagined I'd actually be fighting there."

A move to the historic Rajadamnern Stadium followed soon after, and as his profile continued to grow, he continued to test himself inside the legendary Lumpinee Stadium under the ONE Championship banner.

His promotional bow at ONE Friday Fights 15 in May 2023 did not go to plan, though. Running his entire camp out of Buriram rather than a bigger training hub left him short on the experience needed at that level, and he suffered a narrow decision loss to Sibsan Nokkhao KorMor11 .

Worapon knew a change was needed to compete at that level, and it did not take long before he made the permanent move to Sor Dechapan in Bangkok, a decision that instantly paid off with back-to-back victories on ONE Friday Fights.

It was not just a loss of form. Away from the bright lights, the Thai athlete was dealing with something far heavier, and it showed in the way he carried himself during that stretch.

Whatever internal battles he fought behind the scenes, they did not stop him. Worapon has since returned with a 7-1 run, including three straight victories in 2026 – each one building his case for a life-changing US$100,000 contract.

It has been a long road for the 6-year-old in Buriram, but every stop along the way has shaped the version of Worapon stepping in against Blasi.

articles.title: Potential shirt numbers for Bradley Barcola at Liverpool as £120m transfer on verge of completion
articles.summary: It now seems just a matter of when Bradley Barcola will be officially confirmed as a Liverpool player rather than if.As reported by David Ornstein on Thursda...
articles.body:
It now seems just a matter of when Bradley Barcola will be officially confirmed as a Liverpool player rather than if.

As reported by David Ornstein on Thursday morning, the Reds have reached an 'agreement in principle' with Paris Saint-Germain to sign the winger, with the two clubs understood to have agreed on a deal worth around £120m overall.

Fabrizio Romano subsequently gave the proposed transfer the ' here we go ' treatment, with documents set to be exchanged over the next 24 hours as the formalities of the transaction are carried out.

Assuming there are no late hitches to scupper the deal, Liverpool fans can look forward to seeing Barcola being officially announced as a Red in the coming days, and his name will likely adorn thousands of replica shirts once the transfer is completed.

The accompanying shirt number will also be eagerly anticipated, and while numerous options will be available to the Frenchman, there are two in particular which seem to stand out.

What shirt numbers could Barcola potentially wear at Liverpool?

The winger wears number 29 at PSG, and that shirt is currently free at Anfield, having last been worn by Arthur Melo (for one solitary appearance) four years ago. Prior to that, its most recent occupant was Dominic Solanke in the late 2010s, while Fabio Borini had it between 2012 and 2015.

Barcola will be hoping to leave a greater Liverpool legacy than that trio, none of whom became first-team regulars, but it couldn't be more different for the other number which might seem a logical choice.

The lowest shirt number currently vacant at Anfield is 11, which of course was worn with distinction by the legendary Mo Salah for the past nine years.

The prospective new Reds signing might wish to take it on and accept the challenge of succeeding his illustrious predecessor, or alternatively he might wish to avoid it so that he isn't burdened by obvious comparisons to the Egyptian King.

Barcola wore number 12 for France at the World Cup this summer, but that's currently assigned to Conor Bradley at Liverpool. Numbers 13, 16 and 17 are the next-lowest which are vacant, followed by 24, 26, 27 and 28.

We first need to wait for his proposed transfer to be officially completed, but once that's done, fans can then look forward to seeing which number the Frenchman will adorn at Anfield, in the hope that it'll become as legendary as ' Van Dijk 4' or 'Salah 11'.

articles.title: Arsenal wants to hijack Sunderland transfer
articles.summary: Igor Paixao was close to moving from Olympique Marseille to Sunderland, but Arsenal have joined the race and want to hijack his proposed move to the Stadium...
articles.body:
Igor Paixao was close to moving from Olympique Marseille to Sunderland , but Arsenal have joined the race and want to hijack his proposed move to the Stadium of Light. The Brazilian winger only moved to OM last year, but he enjoyed a strong season and showed that his impressive performances at Feyenoord were not simply because he was playing in the Netherlands.

Paixao has established himself as a top performer, and Sunderland want him to join their squad during this transfer window as they look to strengthen their team. The Premier League club had moved close to completing the transfer, but Arsenal's late interest could now change the situation.

According to Team Talk , Arsenal have reportedly entered the race in the last few hours and want to hijack Sunderland's move as they prepare for Gabriel Martinelli's departure . The report states that the Gunners consider Paixao one of the top players they could add to their attack and would attempt to convince him to abandon the move to Sunderland.

Arsenal's interest comes at a time when they are looking to strengthen their attacking options before the transfer window closes. Paixao's ability on the wing makes him an attractive option, particularly with the Gunners preparing for changes to their attack.

Paixao knows that Arsenal are a bigger club, while the presence of a significant Brazilian contingent at the Emirates could make it easier for him to adapt to life under Mikel Arteta. That connection could give the Gunners an advantage as they attempt to convince the winger to choose them instead of Sunderland.

The circumstances appear favourable for Arsenal to make their case, particularly because Paixao would be joining a club with ambitions to compete for major honours. His previous performances have already demonstrated his quality, and the Gunners believe he could strengthen their attack.

With Martinelli potentially leaving, Arsenal need to bolster their options on the wings before the transfer window closes. Paixao has now emerged as a possible solution, although Sunderland were already close to securing his signature.

The Gunners will therefore need to move quickly if they want to hijack the transfer. Paixao must also be convinced to change his plans, but Arsenal's status and Brazilian presence could help them persuade the 26-year-old to move to north London.

articles.title: New Episode of JaneWallStreet’s ATT: Trailblazing Sports Group Founder Sara Gotfredson
articles.summary: On the latest episode of JaneWallStreet Presents: At The Table, Deirdre Lester sits down with Trailblazing Sports Group Founder Sara Gotfredson. In this hour...
articles.body:
On the latest episode of JaneWallStreet Presents: At The Table , a biweekly podcast exploring the intersection of sports, media and finance through the lens of (mostly) female decision-makers, JaneWallStreet Executive Chair Deirdre Lester sits down with Trailblazing Sports Group (TSG) Founder Sara Gotfredson .

In this hour-long conversation, the two surface and talk through a multitude of actionable insights including:

Women's Sports Outperform on Favorability and Purchase Intent

Brands planning their 2027 media budgets and trying to reach next generation consumers should make women's sports part of the mix. Gen Z represents the fastest-growing segment of the women's sports audience. But the appeal extends beyond who is watching.

"From an ROI perspective, where I see women's sports outkicking their coverage, if you want to use a sports analogy, is in favorability and purchase intent. [Women's sports] are not winning today on the scale game. If [a movie studio] needs mass [audience] within 24 hours to launch a film, [they] should be buying the Super Bowl or AFC championship game. But if [Google is] trying to get people to switch from an iPhone to a Pixel, then [they] need to be showing up again and again in spaces [where fans of women's sports properties exist] because this audience pays back brands that are investing in those [leagues]," Gotfredson said. " 54% of women's sports fans will actually be loyal and purchase a product of the brands that they see showing up again and again in women's sports…We've done a lot of brand research studies when we do campaign [and] those are always the metrics that [shine] for brands."

Winning in Women's Sports Requires a Multichannel Strategy

TSG initially envisioned helping brands enter women's sports through major league and team partnerships. However, the firm has found the most effective marketers are simultaneously investing in a multitude of other channels across the ecosystem.

"There's a lot of data to support that women's sports fans care about the story and the lives of these athletes off the field and off the court, and big media companies aren't always telling those stories. But companies like Togethxr are telling those stories," Gotfredson said. "[So, my advice now is] always a 'yes' and 'yes'. [ As a brand ] you should be doing the league deal. You should be doing the big media deal. [But] you should [also] be supporting the athletes, long tail media, and doing an experiential [activation] at the Women's World Cup in Brazil."

Trio of Olympic Sports Provide an Accessible Entry Point

Zillow's recent partnership with the AUSL highlights the opportunity for brands to secure a prominent position in an ascending women's sports property at an accessible price. But there are at least three other women's sports poised to benefit from the spotlight of the 2028 Summer Olympics.

"When you think about sports that are going to really pop [at] LA28, look at softball, surfing , and flag football," Gotfredson said. "You don't need to have a big nine-figure partnership to show up in a big way with [the pro] leagues [in those sports, either. And doing a tie-up] now, before the buzz of [the Games], is a smart marketing tactic." 📺 Watch the full episode on JohnWallStreet's YouTube page . 🎧 Listen on Apple Podcasts or Spotify .

Catch previous episodes of At The Table , including our sit-down with LOVB Chief Growth Officer Stephanie Alger , former Amazon Web Services' (AWS) Global Head of Sports Julie Souza , Head of Fubo Sports Network & Fubo Studios Pamela Duckworth , former Barstool Sports CEO & Mule Media Co-Founder Erika Badan , ATHLOS Acting President Kayla Green , former CEO of CBS News Wendy McMahon , A-Rod Corp Chief Business Officer & Minnesota Timberwolves Chief Strategy Officer Kelly Laferriere , Rasenberger Media Founder & President Cathy Rasenberger , AUSL Commissioner Kim Ng , and Jomboy Media CEO Courtney Hirsch on JohnWallStreet's YouTube channel.

In the latest episode, The Sports Advisors discuss the U.S. Open and offer some free, unsolicited advice to new USTA President Craig Tiley. Key insights and takeaways from the 55-minute conversation include: screens represent the USTA's most scalable growth opportunity, player access is the next premium frontier, rights owners should choose partners that elevate their events, and creators provide path to the general market.

articles.title: Joe Burrow's comments even get a reply from Marvin Lewis
articles.summary: Even former Bengals head coach Marvin Lewis had something to say about Joe Burrow's comments.
articles.body:
The latest set of comments from Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow created waves of reactions.

Those comments from Burrow were the usual stressing-urgency stuff about the upcoming season. Nothing unusual, with Burrow constantly talking about changing up his leadership style this offseason.

Even so, the comments even earned a reaction from former Bengals head coach Marvin Lewis.

During a sitdown with Trey Wingo , Lewis stressed that Bengals president Mike Brown wants to win and that Burrow's actions will always lead to new approaches.

"His words trigger action," Lewis said. "No question in my mind, they trigger action, because that man loves quarterbacks and he wants to win in the worst way."

It's easy to dismiss this at first glance. The Carson Palmer drama exists. And some of Lewis' examples, like losing Andrew Whitworth, were avoidable mistakes if the organization had been more proactive.

Even so, the Dexter Lawrence trade alongside the rest of the offseason moves hint at another evolution for the franchise. There's little reason to believe Brown and the Bengals won't be the party listening the most intently when Burrow talks, every time.

articles.title: ‘Lane Kiffin Is Already On the Hot Seat’ — LSU Champ Reveals What It’ll Take to Save Coach’s Job Amid Recruiting Controversy

articles.body:
The LSU Tigers are counting on Lane Kiffin's arrival to help restore the program to national prominence and return to the level of success the program expects. However, even before Kiffin coaches his first game of the season, both he and LSU are facing criticism because of the ongoing recruiting controversy.

Former LSU star Breiden Fehoko , who was part of the Tigers' undefeated 2019 national championship team, has now weighed in on Kiffin's situation and delivered a blunt warning about what the coach needs to accomplish to secure his position.

Breiden Fehoko Reveals What Lane Kiffin Must Do to Save His Job

Kiffin and LSU are currently trying to add at least three players who were recently released from NFL training camps but have since obtained temporary restraining orders from an East Baton Rouge Parish judge allowing them to compete.

Amid the controversy, Fehoko took to X to criticize Kiffin and outline what he believes the LSU coach must accomplish to avoid serious pressure.

"LSU fans hate hearing the truth, but yes, Lane Kiffin is already on the hot seat, whether you like me or not," Fehoko wrote . "You left Ole Miss cause they couldn't give you what LSU has to offer. So it's fair to say at the very minimum we need a playoff appearance this year."

In the video, Fehoko dismissed the idea that Kiffin should be given several years to build the program, using Indiana coach Curt Cignetti's success last season as an example.

Fehoko specifically argued that a program with a $40 million roster should have a realistic expectation of reaching the playoffs in Kiffin's first season.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

LSU fired Brian Kelly in October. The program subsequently turned to Kiffin, hiring the former Ole Miss head coach on a seven-year, $91 million contract.

Since arriving in Baton Rouge, Kiffin has aggressively reshaped LSU's roster. The Tigers brought in a transfer class that recruiting analysts have ranked among the strongest in the country.

Several reports have labeled LSU as the most expensive roster in college football heading into 2026.

LSU is a proud program that carries national championship expectations every season. With Kiffin now in charge of one of the most talented and expensive rosters in college football, the pressure to deliver results will be enormous, and meeting those expectations will be no easy task.

articles.title: Liverpool closing in on deal for PSG's Barcola

articles.body:
Liverpool have reached an outline agreement with Paris Saint-Germain for Bradley Barcola worth up to £120 million ($162.9 million), the Press Association understands.

The Reds have been pursuing a deal for the 23-year-old France winger and made a breakthrough in talks on Wednesday.

A guaranteed fee just over £100 million has been agreed in principle along with add-ons that could take the package up to £120 million, but there remains work to do to complete the deal as details are ironed out.

PSG had initially wanted in the region of £145 million for Barcola, who spent June and July at the World Cup with France and scored three goals.

Barcola joined the perennial French champions from Lyon in 2023 and was part of their back-to-back Champions League triumphs.

Liverpool are working to improve their wide options before Tuesday's transfer deadline after club great Mohamed Salah departed.

The Anfield outfit have explored a move for Crystal Palace 's Ismaila Sarr and last week saw two bids rejected by Brighton for Yankuba Minteh , with the second offer worth £60 million.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola is set to speak to the media on Thursday at the press conference previewing Saturday's Anfield encounter against Nottingham Forest .

articles.title: Ex-Baggie Barnes had 'some of best moments' at Albion
articles.summary: Newcastle winger Harvey Barnes says he had some of his career-best moments on loan at West Brom despite knocking them out of the EFL Cup.
articles.body:
Newcastle United winger Harvey Barnes ruined West Bromwich Albion's night on Tyneside as he came off the bench at half-time to score twice and send the Magpies through to the third round of the Carabao Cup.

The hosts' thrilling 3-2 win ended the chance of James Morrison becoming the first Albion boss to win his first four matches of the season since 1947.

But Barnes was gracious enough in victory to acknowledge the part his old club played in his own career trajectory.

Barnes' two goals took his career tally with Leicester, Newcastle and his three loan spells at MK Dons, Barnsley and the Baggies to 97 - but it was at The Hawthorns in the first half of the 2018-19 season where he really took off, fashioning nine goals and eight assists in 28 appearances for Darren Moore's promotion-chasing side.

"Mozza [Morrison] was part of the squad then," recalls Barnes. "It's a bit weird seeing him as a manager now. But I have really fond memories. I loved it when I got sent to West Brom.

"For pure football, and excitement wise, it was some of the best moments I've had in my career. With the football we played and the team we had, the environment was perfect for any young player to go and thrive in.

"I didn't want to come back from my loan, I was enjoying it that much, but it was out of my hands."

Albion are staying on in the North East for Saturday's meeting with Middlesbrough as they attempt to maintain their 100% start to the Championship season.

They do so with one of the most in-form players in the country in their line-up, midfielder Isaac Price having followed up his brace in Sunday's 3-1 win over Burnley on Sunday with another double.

Four goals in two games, including two nerveless penalties, is a spectacular return to scoring form for the Yorkshire-born Northern Ireland international, who netted 10 times for the Baggies last season.

And Morrison says that Price's output is the product of the current surge of belief running through his squad.

"I was confident that we could cause them some problems," he said. "I gave the players the belief and showed them that we could go there and cause those problems. I don't want us to go to places and sit back. I want us to go and impose ourselves.

"Going to places like Newcastle, you have to manage momentum. They came out of the blocks really quickly in the opening 10 minutes and we had to get through it. I was a bit disappointed with the timing of the second goal, right at the start of the second half. However, we came back into it, we competed and we played some nice stuff."

articles.title: 'We can build something really strong' - Delap completes Forest switch
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest record signing Liam Delap believes Oliver Glasner can be the coach to "really help me develop and get to that next step".  Delap has comple...
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest record signing Liam Delap believes Oliver Glasner can be the coach to "really help me develop and get to that next step".

Delap has completed a £50m transfer from Chelsea and signed a five-year deal at the City Ground after just one season at Stamford Bridge.

The 23-year-old striker struggled in west London, scoring just one league goal, but was convinced of the Forest project by new head coach Glasner, who himself arrived earlier this summer.

"I really can't wait to get started, it's a massive club with a big history so I can't wait.

"I spoke with the head coach and I really like his way. I think he can be the one to really help me develop and get to that next step. There're some top players here as well and I'm looking forward to playing alongside them."

Delap scored 12 goals for Ipswich Town in his first Premier League campaign in 2024-25 in a side that only won four games all season and were relegated in 19th place.

"It was probably the time when I've enjoyed playing football the most and I think that was when I played my best football as well," he added.

"I'm aggressive and I play with a lot of speed and aggression. Hopefully I can bring some goals here as well.

"With the new head coach I think we can build something really strong. The main aim is to challenge and be a top club in the Premier League."

articles.title: All schedules are not created equal. Which CT football teams will be helped, hurt most by theirs.
articles.summary: We break down 10 high school football teams whose schedules could have a major impact on their playoff chances.
articles.body:
With six high school football playoff divisions in the CIAC , the margin between reaching the postseason and being left out can be razor thin.

Sometimes, that margin starts with the schedule.

Over the years, we've seen very good teams draw difficult slates, finish around .500 and wind up on the outside of the CIAC playoffs. We've also seen teams benefit from more manageable schedules that provide a greater margin for error.

That doesn't mean a playoff berth is handed to anyone. It just means some roads are considerably tougher than others.

Not all schedules are created equally, so GametimeCT's Will Aldam and Pete Paguaga took a look at five teams that could be hurt by difficult schedules and five that should benefit from more favorable ones.

Five teams who could be hurt by schedule

Could win: West Haven, Glastonbury, Notre Dame-West Haven, Staples, Jonathan Law, Sheehan

West Haven, Glastonbury, Notre Dame-West Haven, Staples, Jonathan Law, Sheehan

Toss-up: Hand, Fairfield Prep, Southington

Cheshire reached the CIAC Class L championship game and fell to New Canaan 34-13. The Rams return a number of starters from last year's run, but graduated All-State QB/LB Aiden Gregorich and now face one of the most difficult schedules in the state. Its opponents had a combined record of 80-36 (.690) last year, and the group includes two defending state champions, a runner-up and a semifinalist. Nine of Cheshire's 10 opponents reached the playoffs last year.

Toss-up: Fairfield Ludlowe, Glastonbury, New Britain, Southington, Berlin, Windsor

Fairfield Ludlowe, Glastonbury, New Britain, Southington, Berlin, Windsor

Enfield finished just 25 power points out of a 2025 Class L playoff berth at 6-4. Now the Eagles move up to Tier 1 of the CCC this year, which means a tougher schedule that includes six opponents who reached the CIAC playoffs last year, including two defending state champions and a runner-up. Enfield is set up well with its 11 returning starters, including All-Conference quarterback Sawyer Pequita and two-time All-State lineman Joel Budd. Enfield's 2026 season will certainly be one to follow.

Should win: Manchester, Conard, Simsbury

Toss-up: Cheshire, St. Joseph, New Britain, Southington, Windsor

Cheshire, St. Joseph, New Britain, Southington, Windsor

Glastonbury reached the CIAC Class LL quarterfinals last year before falling to Southington 35-30. Glastonbury returns star running back Dante Casdia, but graduated several other starters. The Guardians have one of the toughest schedules in the state this year. Five opponents reached the postseason last year, a group that includes a defending state champion, two runners-up and a semifinalist.

For a team replacing significant experience, that's not exactly a gentle runway back to the playoffs.

Could win: Jonathan Law, Ludlowe, North Haven

Toss-up: Cheshire, Sheehan, Hand, Fairfield Prep, New Britain

Cheshire, Sheehan, Hand, Fairfield Prep, New Britain

West Haven narrowly missed out on the Class LL tournament last year after reaching back-to-back state finals. A difficult schedule won't make it any easier. The Blue Devils' 2026 opponents went a combined 84-31 last season, a .730 winning percentage. Eight reached the postseason, including two defending state champions, a state runner-up and a semifinalist. West Haven also has to replace significant production at quarterback and running back as coach Tom Unger enters his second season.

Toss-up: Berlin, Southington, St. Joseph, Greenwich, New Canaan

Berlin, Southington, St. Joseph, Greenwich, New Canaan

Wilton is coming off a terrific season that ended in the CIAC Class MM semifinals. The Warriors graduated quarterback Charlie Calabrese and three of his top receivers, but star running back Dennis Dustin returns. The bigger concern may be a schedule that gets progressively more difficult. Seven opponents reached the postseason last year, and early November brings back-to-back games against four-time defending Class L champion New Canaan and two-time defending Class LL champion Greenwich. Then again, Wilton has beaten Greenwich in each of the past two seasons.

Should win: Ledyard, New Milford, Hillhouse, East Haven

Lyman Hall carries a lot of memories from last season. The Trojans just missed out on a state playoff berth and it wasn't because they didn't win enough games. They won seven. But their schedule didn't help their point total and they were faced with a win-and-in scenario on Thanksgiving morning, a game they lost to Sheehan. Once again, the Trojans schedule doesn't look daunting to start, with just two playoff teams (Ledyard and Guilford) in the first seven games. All seven of those games could/should be won by the Trojans, who bring back a bunch of talent led by quarterback Ryan Casey. There is a very real path to another seven-win season before the schedule gets challenging, with games against Hand, Law and Sheehan, teams they are a combined 10-31 against since 2004. They will likely need to beat one of them to get in. Good luck Trojans.

Should win: New Fairfield, Pomperaug, Notre Dame-Prep, Joel Barlow, New Milford, Brookfield, Masuk

New Fairfield, Pomperaug, Notre Dame-Prep, Joel Barlow, New Milford, Brookfield, Masuk

Newtown , Newtown, Newtown the Alliance can't do all of the work for you. This is not meant as a knock on the SWC at all, but you have to wonder if Newtown has outgrown the rest of the league. Over the last five seasons, Newtown has lost 13 games, only two of those have come to an SWC team, both Masuk. With eight SWC games on the schedule and Alliance games against Southington and Greenwich, there is a realistic path to eight wins, potentially nine.

Should win: Tolland, Cheney/Windham Tech, RHAM, Lewis Mills/Wolcott Tech, East Catholic, Avon/St. Paul

Tolland, Cheney/Windham Tech, RHAM, Lewis Mills/Wolcott Tech, East Catholic, Avon/St. Paul

Could win: Middletown, Northwest Catholic, Plainville

Middletown, Northwest Catholic, Plainville

The Terriers took big strides last year to get to 5-5 with a young group and look to take a step forward this season. With a schedule like theirs, a step forward is very realistic. Over the past five seasons, Rocky Hill has losing records against Northwest Catholic (2-3), Plainville (0-2), RHAM (0-1) and Cromwell/Portland (0-5). The Terriers have winning records against five other teams on this year's schedule and have not faced Cheney/Windham Tech during that span. Led by Tyshawn Dominique and quarterback Mason Margiotta, Rocky Hill has a legitimate chance to pile up wins before the annual Shunpike Showdown against Cromwell/Portland.

Should win: Crosby, Norwalk, Danbury, McMahon, Warde

Crosby, Norwalk, Danbury, McMahon, Warde

The Golden Eagles are pumped for this season and after looking at their schedule, they should be excited. Only two of the FCIAC's traditional heavyweights, New Canaan and St. Joseph, appear on the slate, and those games bookend Trumbull's season. Their Alliance games are against Crosby of the NVL and Shelton of the SCC. The Gaels have also fallen on tough times. Against its six FCIAC opponents not named New Canaan or St. Joseph, Trumbull has gone a combined 14-1 over the past five seasons. That figure does not include Norwalk, which the Golden Eagles haven't faced since 2019. Trumbull has a lot to fix after a 3-7 season, but after its opener against New Canaan, the Eagles should be in cruise control until November when they get Fairfield Ludlowe and St. Joseph in two of the final three games.

Should win: Kennedy, Crosby, Oxford, Wilby, Wolcott, Watertown

The Naugatuck Valley League finally joined the Alliance to help their teams better prepare for the state playoffs, but still the league scheduling still doesn't make sense. The league adopted a power scheduling model and some teams reap the benefits. Almost every year, Torrington seems to be one of them. Just two of its opponents had winning records last year: NVL power Ansonia, which is 13-0 against Torrington since 2004, and Fitch of the Eastern Connecticut Conference. Against eight of its other 2026 opponents last season, Torrington went 7-1 and outscored them 334-115. The Raiders scored at least 39 points in each of those seven victories. Their lone loss in that group was a 20-16 game against Naugatuck. Torrington is looking at eight to nine wins this season.
